In 1968 the two governments set up the Eilat Ashkelon Pipeline Company as a 50/50 joint venture, so secret that Israel's confidentiality order on it was still being renewed in January 2023. [cite:wiki_eapc] Iranian oil kept reaching Israel during the 1973 war. The alliance itself followed the 1953 CIA–MI6 coup that restored the Shah; Israel had no documented role in that coup. [cite:nsarchive_cia_confirms_role]

The revolution turned the pipeline into a legal dispute; in 2016 a tribunal ordered Israel to pay Iran over $1.1 billion. Yet Israel still sold the Islamic Republic roughly $500 million in arms between 1980 and 1983, mostly paid for in oil. [cite:wiki_iran_israel_relations] In 1982 Defense Minister Ariel Sharon said Israel had "a vital interest" in "Iran's victory" over Iraq. On August 20, 1985, Israel delivered 100 American-made TOW missiles to Iran, a deal that became part of the Iran-Contra affair. [cite:jewishcurrents_israel_sells_iran] The open enmity is real, but it is newer than the line suggests.

Read more [scene:ira_s01|Volume XXII, The Iran Architecture: The Pipeline Israel Kept Secret for Fifty Years] · [scene:ira_s02|Volume XXII, The Iran Architecture: Enemies on Paper, Arms Dealers in Practice] (volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

Hamas, Hezbollah and the Houthis are just Iranian proxies with no causes of their own.

Misleading

Iran's backing of all three groups is well documented, but each has its own origin, and calling them "just proxies" erases it. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Qods Force has funded, armed and trained Hamas for decades, with reported figures ranging from $22–70 million a year historically to $350 million by 2023, per Israeli security sources. [cite:congress_iran_hamas_testimony] Yet Hamas, a Sunni movement, was historically wary of taking too much money from the region's dominant Shia power. [cite:jstribune_hamas_iran_relationship] It was founded in 1987 during the first intifada, after twenty years of occupation.

Hezbollah formed after Israel's 1982 invasion of Lebanon, with about 1,500 Revolutionary Guard instructors, and its first aim was ending the occupation of the south. Former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak said in 2006 that "it was our presence there that created Hezbollah"; an Israeli research center argues Iran was the founding cause. [cite:wiki_hezbollah_mirror] [cite:terrorism_info_hezbollah_birth] The Houthis grew from a 1990s Zaydi revival and fought Yemen's government and a Saudi-led coalition long before attacking Israel. The frame is right about alignment and selective about causes.

Read more [scene:ye_s07|Volume LVII, Israel-Yemen Architecture: The 'Proxy' Frame] · [scene:sq_s03|Volume LXVI, Street Questions: 'Hezbollah Just Hates Israel'] (volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

The Abraham Accords brought peace to the Middle East.

Half true

The Abraham Accords produced normalization, not an end to any war. Between August and December 2020, Israel normalized relations with the UAE, Bahrain, Sudan and Morocco, none of which had fought it or shared a border with it. [cite:wiki_abraham_accords] Each deal carried a US reward: approval of a roughly $23 billion F-35 and drone sale for the UAE, security guarantees for Bahrain, recognition of Morocco's claim to Western Sahara, and Sudan's removal from the terrorism list. [cite:wiki_uae_israel_normalization] [cite:brit_abraham]

The gains are real: a free-trade agreement, over $3.2 billion in annual goods trade, flights that continued through the Gaza war, and, by Emirati account, a suspension of annexation plans in 2020. [cite:ac_accords5] [cite:cnn_redline] But Palestinians were sidelined in all four deals, and there has been no movement toward a Palestinian state. The deals were decided at the top, protests followed in Morocco and Bahrain, and no signatory has left. Supporters call that endurance proof; critics call it the problem. [cite:passblue_accords] [cite:fp_accords_conflict]

Read more [scene:ae_s09|Volume LVIII, Israel-UAE Architecture: What Normalization Delivered] · [scene:oa_s08|Volume LIX, The Other Accords: The Ledger] (volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

sections.h: America: money, aid and the message
sections.html:
Lines about US aid, the pro-Israel lobby, and where the talking points themselves come from.

AIPAC is just an ordinary lobby like any other.

Misleading

AIPAC is a legal, American-funded lobby, but its scale and history are not ordinary. Founded in 1953 and operating as a 501(c)(4), it does not take money from foreign governments; its funding comes from American donors [cite:israellobby_org_fara_doj_order]. What sets it apart is the money around it: pro-Israel PAC spending rose from about $25M in 2020 to about $43M in 2022 and over $100M in 2024, much of it through the United Democracy Project, the super PAC AIPAC launched in December 2021 [cite:opensecrets_udp] [cite:opensecrets_pro_israel_pacs]. In 2024 that super PAC spent about $14.5M against Rep. Jamaal Bowman and about $8.5M against Rep. Cori Bush in their primaries, and both lost [cite:wiki_bowman_primary_2024] [cite:factcheck_udp_2024].

The history is unusual too. On November 21, 1962, Robert Kennedy's Justice Department ordered AIPAC's parent body, the American Zionist Council, to register as a foreign agent after it received $5,100,001.02 from the Jewish Agency for Israel between 1955 and 1962 [cite:israellobby_org_fara_doj_order] [cite:jta_fulbright_jewish_agency_hearing]. All of this is documented lobbying in public filings, not a hidden operation.

Read more [scene:s19b|Volume VI, The Machine, Named: The Money, Named] · [scene:s19|Volume VI, The Machine, Named: The Heritage / AIPAC Machine] (volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

AIPAC money buys Congress.

Depends on what's said

The record shows heavy, legal spending to reward allies and defeat opponents; it does not show votes being bought. Federal law bars foreign governments and foreign nationals from giving in any US election, so the money in campaign filings comes from American donors and American PACs [cite:fec_foreign_nationals]. AIPAC itself gave nothing to candidates until it created a PAC and the United Democracy Project super PAC in late 2021 [cite:opensecrets_aipac_2019]. Since then the scale has been large: pro-Israel PAC spending reached over $100M in 2024, including about $14.5M against Rep. Jamaal Bowman and about $8.5M against Rep. Cori Bush, both of whom lost their primaries [cite:opensecrets_udp] [cite:factcheck_udp_2024].

Whether money changes votes is harder to show. A Guardian analysis found that members who took more pro-Israel money more often backed military support for Israel, but party, not money, best predicted their statements on civilian casualties [cite:guardian_gaza_donors]. Before 1971, candidates' donors were largely undisclosed, so claims of systematic payments to members of Congress before 1948 cannot be proved or disproved [cite:wiki_fcpa_1925].

Read more [scene:mn_s02|Volume II, The Road to 1948: Did Money Buy the Politicians? What the Pre-1948 Record Can Show] · [scene:cm_s00|Volume VII, Pro-Israel Money in Congress: Read This First] (one volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

Without US aid, Israel couldn't defend itself.

False

Israel's own spending dwarfs the US aid it receives. Under the current agreement the US provides $3.8B a year from 2019 to 2028 [cite:washington_inst_mou], while Israel spent an estimated $52 billion on its own defense in 2025 and budgeted roughly $49 billion for 2026, about 13 to 14 times the aid [cite:israelpolicyforum_aid]. Israel's own INSS puts the aid at about 0.6% of GDP and says it could be absorbed, and Israel earned $14.8B from arms exports in 2024, roughly three times the aid [cite:inss_us_aid] [cite:sipri_arms].

Supporters of the aid say much the same. Israel Policy Forum, which backs continued cooperation, says Israel was "clearly capable" of covering regular peacetime defense costs without it before October 2023, and Prime Minister Netanyahu has proposed phasing the aid out [cite:israelpolicyforum_aid] [cite:fdd_netanyahu_aid]. One caveat: wartime spending has run higher, and Israel's 2026 defense increase came alongside cuts to education, health and welfare.

Read more [scene:usil_s09|Volume XLVII, US ⇄ Israel: Defense, GDP, and the $3.8 Billion Question] · [scene:s19f|Volume VI, The Machine, Named: $3.8 Billion] (volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

Aid to Israel all gets spent in America anyway.

True, with limits

Most of it is, and by 2028 nearly all of it will be, but "all" and "always" go too far. The 2016 agreement pledged $38 billion for FY2019–2028 and phases out "off-shore procurement," so that military financing is spent on American goods and services [cite:israeled_mou_text] [cite:crs_aid_israel_2016]. About 80% of the roughly $23 billion in post-October 7 aid has gone to American weapons makers such as Boeing, Lockheed Martin, RTX and General Dynamics [cite:aid_costsofwar].

The limits matter. For four decades Israel alone was allowed to spend up to roughly 26% of its aid on its own arms industry, benefiting named firms such as Israel Aerospace Industries and Elbit Systems; that exception is only now winding down to zero by 2028 [cite:spencerguard_38billion_israel] [cite:crs_us_foreign_aid_israel_2023]. For missile defense, the agreement sets a goal of at least 50% US co-production, not all of it [cite:israeled_mou_text]. Israel also receives its aid as a lump sum within 30 days, placed in an interest-bearing Federal Reserve account [cite:internationalpolicy_israel_security_partnership].

Read more [scene:iaa_s02|Volume XXVI, Israel Aid Architecture: The Money That Doesn't Leave] · [scene:wlg_s01|Volume XXIII, The War Ledger: The Money That Doesn't Leave] (volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

Pro-Israel posts online are just ordinary people; nobody is paid.

False

Israel's own government has paid for online campaigns aimed at Americans, and its filings say so. A September 26, 2025 filing under the Foreign Agents Registration Act shows Israel's Foreign Ministry funding the "Esther Project," up to $900,000 from June to November 2025, through a firm called Bridges Partners, to recruit 14–18 US influencers posting 25–30 times a month [cite:jpost_esther] [cite:wiki_esther_project]. TIME reported group chats in which influencers were coached on wording and paid up to $4,250 per post; their names are still undisclosed [cite:mee_esther_backfire] [cite:rs_paid_influencers]. Earlier, per the New York Times, Israel's Diaspora Affairs Ministry paid about $2 million to a firm called STOIC to run fake accounts posing as Americans; Meta removed 510 Facebook and 32 Instagram accounts. The ministry denied involvement [cite:toi_stoic].

That does not mean every pro-Israel post is paid. Many people sincerely hold these views, and the companies said STOIC gained little traction [cite:cyberscoop_stoic]. Influence campaigns also run the other way: an Iran-linked network used fake profiles to stir tensions inside Israel [cite:calcalist_iran_social_media_network].

Read more [scene:ip_s01|Volume VIII, Pro-Israel Voices in America: The 'Esther Project'] · [scene:sk_s01|Volume I, The Baseline: Where the Talking Points Come From] (one volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

The UN is biased against Israel.

Half true

Israel is singled out in some UN bodies and shielded in the one that can issue binding decisions; the line cites only the first half. At the Human Rights Council, Item 7, on the human rights situation in Palestine and other occupied Arab territories, is the only country-specific item on the permanent agenda, and Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon voiced disappointment at the decision to single out Israel [cite:unwatch_item7]. UN Watch, a pro-Israel watchdog, counts 17 General Assembly resolutions on Israel in 2024 against 7 on all other countries combined [cite:unwatch_unga2024].

The other half: the United States has vetoed Security Council resolutions critical of Israel 45 times as of December 2023, slightly over half of its 89 vetoes since 1945 [cite:ccga_vetoes]. Many General Assembly resolutions also concern the occupation since 1967 and the UN's own role since Resolution 181 in 1947. Whether the volume of resolutions reflects bias, the length of the occupation, or both is the real argument.

Read more [scene:sk_s04|Volume LXVI, Street Questions: Is the UN Biased Against Israel? The Case For] (volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

sections.h: Antisemitism and criticism of Israel
sections.html:
Lines about where criticism of a state ends and hatred of Jews begins.

Anti-Zionism is antisemitism.

Depends on what's said

The answer depends on which definition is used, and the leading definitions disagree. The 2016 IHRA working definition, adopted by the US government and, as of August 2024, by 35 states and the District of Columbia, lists "denying the Jewish people their right to self-determination" as a potential example of antisemitism; seven of its 11 examples concern Israel [cite:reformjudaism_five_definitions] [cite:peacenow_ihra_faq]. The Jerusalem Declaration of March 2021, signed by more than 200 scholars of Jewish history and the Holocaust, holds that anti-Zionism is not antisemitic on its face, while listing examples that are; the Nexus Document sits between the two [cite:jwa_jda] [cite:thirdnarrative_three_defs].

Both concerns in this argument are real. IHRA's lead drafter, Kenneth Stern, says it has been weaponized against critics of Israel [cite:stern_guardian_2019], while Britain's Community Security Trust says the Jerusalem Declaration legitimizes calls for Israel's elimination [cite:cst_jda_critique]. Some anti-Zionist speech does cross into hatred of Jews, and the ADL recorded a record 9,354 US antisemitic incidents in 2024 [cite:algemeiner_adl_2024]. The practical test is the target: a state's policies, or Jewish people.

Read more [scene:az_s01|Volume I, The Baseline: Is Anti-Zionism Antisemitism? Three Competing Definitions] · [scene:s00b1|Volume I, The Baseline: The Shield]

Any criticism of Israel is antisemitic.

False

Even the definition most governments use says the opposite. The IHRA working definition, which the State Department has used in some form since 2010, states in its own text that "criticism of Israel similar to that leveled against any other country cannot be regarded as antisemitic" [cite:state_defining_antisemitism] [cite:ihra_text_safeguard]. Its lead drafter, Kenneth Stern, has said it was never intended to chill speech, and in a December 2019 Guardian op-ed warned that it was being weaponized against critics of Israel [cite:stern_guardian_2019]. The ACLU has warned that equating criticism of Israel's government with antisemitism chills speech [cite:politifact_aaa_2024].

Antisemitism, meaning hatred of Jews, is still real: the ADL counted 9,354 US incidents in 2024, the most since it began counting in 1979. Some speech that calls itself criticism of Israel does cross that line. The test the definition itself sets: is the criticism aimed at a government's actions, and would it be fair if aimed at any other country? Or is it aimed at Jews as a people, holding them responsible for a state?

Read more [scene:s00b1|Volume I, The Baseline: The Shield] · [scene:df_s07|Volume XVIII, The Domestic Footprint: The State Department's Antisemitism Definition] (one volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

Zionism is Judaism, so opposing Zionism means opposing Jews.

False

Judaism is an ancient religion and set of ethnic-cultural lineages; Zionism is a political movement founded in Basel in August 1897 by Theodor Herzl, a secular Viennese journalist. Herzl himself wrote in his diary, "At Basel I founded the Jewish State," and he considered Argentina and Uganda before Palestine was settled on [cite:herzl_diaries]. Jewish opposition to political Zionism is documented from the start: American Reform Judaism's 1885 Pittsburgh Platform declared Jews "no longer a nation, but a religious community" [cite:pittsburgh_platform_1885], and the Jewish Labor Bund, founded in Vilna in 1897, rejected emigration to Palestine [cite:wiki_bund].

Today Satmar, the largest Hasidic dynasty, still teaches Rabbi Joel Teitelbaum's 1958 case against a Jewish state [cite:wiki_satmar], and Mizrahi scholars such as Ella Shohat and Sami Shalom Chetrit have built their own critique of the state [cite:chetrit_mizrahi_struggle]. Jewish views also form a spectrum: Martin Buber and Judah Magnes were Zionists who rejected partition. Zionism has always been a contested position within Jewish life, so opposing it is not, by itself, opposing Jews.

Read more [scene:s00c|Volume I, The Baseline: Zionism ≠ Judaism] · [scene:s00b3|Volume I, The Baseline: Opposition to Zionism Cuts Across Every Lineage]

Free Palestine is just code for antisemitism.

Misleading

"Free Palestine" is a political position, and the record of who says it contradicts the idea that it is always code for hatred of Jews. Jewish organizations such as Jewish Voice for Peace campaign for Palestinian rights [cite:w_jvp], Orthodox anti-Zionist traditions are older than the state of Israel, and Israeli human-rights groups such as B'Tselem document the occupation. A slogan used by these groups and by many Jewish Americans cannot, by itself, be proof of antisemitism.

There is a real kernel in the worry. Some people who use the slogan do express antisemitism, and those incidents are documented. Where criticism of a state ends and hostility toward a people begins is a subject of genuine debate. The fair test is the one the record supports: judge what a person actually says and does, not the slogan they chant.

Read more [scene:cmt_s09|Volume I, The Baseline: "'Free Palestine' Is Just Code for Antisemitism"]

BDS is an antisemitic movement.

Depends on what's said

BDS is a boycott campaign with stated political demands; whether those demands are acceptable is the real dispute. It was launched on 9 July 2005 by about 170 Palestinian unions, refugee networks and civil-society groups, modeled on the anti-apartheid boycott, with three demands: end the occupation of Arab lands, full equality for Israel's Arab-Palestinian citizens, and a right of return for refugees under Resolution 194 [cite:bds_call]. The movement says it opposes all racism, including antisemitism.

Critics' strongest point is not the tactic but the goal: they argue a full right of return for refugees and descendants would end Israel's Jewish majority, and that "Arab lands" can be read as all of Israel [cite:wm_bds] [cite:fdd_bds]. By early 2024, 38 US states had taken measures against BDS, mostly barring state contracts with companies that boycott Israel [cite:britannica_bds]. Courts are split: four federal courts found such laws likely unconstitutional, while in February 2023 the Supreme Court declined to hear an appeal of a ruling upholding Arkansas's law [cite:pl_antiboycott].

Read more [scene:gx_s03|Volume LXVI, Street Questions: What Is BDS? The 2005 Call, the Three Demands, and 38 States' Laws Against It] (volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

sections.h: Lines aimed the other way
sections.html:
Lines that target Jews or lean on old antisemitic tropes, held to the same standard as every other line here.

Ashkenazi Jews are really Khazars with no tie to the land.

False, aimed the other way

The genetic studies that tested this claim found no evidence for it. The Khazars were a Turkic people whose rulers adopted Judaism around the 8th century, and a 2012 paper by geneticist Eran Elhaik argued they were a major source of Ashkenazi ancestry; critics faulted its use of modern Armenians and Georgians as stand-ins for Khazars [cite:adl_khazar] [cite:aap_khazar_factcheck]. A 2013 study in Human Biology, analyzing 1,774 samples from 106 populations including the Khazar region, found no particular similarity with Caucasus populations and traced Ashkenazi ancestry primarily to the Middle East and Europe [cite:behar_2013_khazar] [cite:nli_behar_khazar]. A 2010 Nature study of 14 Jewish communities found most cluster closer to each other and to Middle Eastern populations than to their host populations [cite:behar_2010_nature].

The kernel of truth is real European ancestry, substantial on the maternal line; one researcher puts the Middle Eastern share at 15–50%. The Khazar theory has been used since the 19th century to cast Jews as impostors [cite:jewishpress_khazar]. And genetics settles no one's political rights, Jewish or Palestinian.

Read more [scene:kh_s01|Volume I, The Baseline: 'Ashkenazi Jews Are Really Khazars'] · [scene:s00b2|Volume I, The Baseline: The Jewish Lineages]

Jews were gone from the land for 2,000 years until Zionism.

False, aimed the other way

A smaller Jewish community remained in the land without a break, though for most of those centuries it was a minority. After crushing the Bar Kokhba revolt (132–135 CE), Rome killed, enslaved or expelled much of Judea's Jewish population, barred Jews from Jerusalem, rebuilt it as Aelia Capitolina and renamed the province Syria Palaestina [cite:wiki_syria_palaestina]. But a continuous Jewish presence stayed on, with Galilee as its religious center, where much classical Jewish literature was produced. In the 16th century Jewish communities took root in Jerusalem, Hebron, Tiberias and Safed, forming the pre-Zionist "Old Yishuv," a minority that fluctuated in size [cite:encyclo_israel_history].

The kernel of truth is that the Jewish population shrank sharply and the majority became Arabic-speaking Muslims and Christians, the ancestors of today's Palestinians, under Byzantine, Muslim, Crusader, Mamluk and Ottoman rule [cite:wiki_palestine_region]. Both histories are documented, and neither erases the other.

Read more [scene:ah_s01|Volume I, The Baseline: Start Here: 3,000 Years in One Scene]

The Rothschilds paid for Zionism; Herzl's movement was their project.

Misleading

Rothschild money built early settlements, but the political movement that became the state was launched after a Rothschild refused to back it. From 1882, after the Russian pogroms, Baron Edmond de Rothschild financed roughly thirty Jewish agricultural colonies in Ottoman Palestine, including Rishon LeZion and Zikhron Ya'akov [cite:wiki_edmond_james_de_rothschild]. That is the kernel of truth: Ben-Gurion later called him the "builder of the Jewish Yishuv" [cite:betweenmyths_rothschild_israel]. But in July 1896 Theodor Herzl asked Edmond to back political Zionism and was turned down; Herzl's own diary records that "from Rothschild's negative attitude I must salvage everything" [cite:herzl_diaries_vol2_archive]. The First Zionist Congress met in Basel in 1897 without him.

Herzl's movement then built its own bank, the Jewish Colonial Trust of 1899, on £1 shares sold in installments so ordinary people could buy in; about 250,000 shares sold [cite:jct_wiki]. Later funding came from mass giving: the 1948 United Jewish Appeal raised a record $150 million from more than a million contributors [cite:jta_uja_1948].

Read more [scene:bc_s04|Volume II, The Road to 1948: The Baron Who Built the Colonies] · [scene:s04c|Volume II, The Road to 1948: The Jewish Colonial Trust: Zionism Gets a Bank]

Six million is a made-up round number nobody can verify.

False, aimed the other way

The figure is verified through several independent methods that converge on the same range, and the Holocaust is the best-documented genocide in history [cite:ushmm_evidence_documentation]. Historian Raul Hilberg's demographic breakdown estimated 5.1 million Jewish deaths; Lucy Dawidowicz's 1975 research into prewar birth and death records produced 5,933,900 [cite:wiki_destruction_european_jews]. Yad Vashem's ongoing Book of Names project has individually identified about 4.8 million victims by name, and the work continues [cite:wiki_book_of_names]. At Auschwitz alone, at least 1.1 million people were murdered [cite:wiki_auschwitz_camp].

The perpetrators' own paperwork is part of the record. On July 31, 1941, Hermann Göring ordered Reinhard Heydrich to prepare the "Final Solution" [cite:yadvashem_wannsee_final_solution], and the Wannsee Protocol of January 20, 1942, listing about 11 million Jews across Europe, later became evidence at Nuremberg and at Eichmann's 1961 trial [cite:ushmm_wannsee_protocol]. The kernel of truth is only that "six million" is a rounded figure: scholars' estimates differ in detail, but they all fall in the same range.

Read more [scene:hol_s05|Volume II, The Road to 1948: The Documented Scale] · [scene:hol_s04|Volume II, The Road to 1948: Wannsee]

The Zionists collaborated with the Nazis.

Misleading

The record holds two real episodes, and neither amounts to the movement siding with Nazism. On 25 August 1933 the Zionist Federation of Germany and the Anglo-Palestine Bank, acting for the Jewish Agency, signed the Haavara ("transfer") Agreement with the Reich Economics Ministry, letting emigrating German Jews move part of their assets to Palestine as German export goods [cite:wiki_haavara_agreement]. About 60,000 German Jews reached Palestine through it between 1933 and 1939, but it also undercut the worldwide anti-Nazi boycott. Jabotinsky, Rabbi Stephen Wise and Abba Hillel Silver opposed it, and the 1935 Zionist Congress voted by a large majority to continue it [cite:jvl_haavara]. It was both a rescue and a commercial accommodation.

Separately, a document dated 11 January 1941 records an offer by the Lehi underground, a militant fringe group, to fight on Germany's side in exchange for support for a Jewish state; no German reply is recorded [cite:marxists_ankara_document]. The mainstream Zionist Executive denounced Lehi and the Irgun as "traitors" [cite:daat_moyne].

Read more [scene:hv_s01|Volume II, The Road to 1948: The Transfer Agreement] · [scene:lh_s01|Volume II, The Road to 1948: The Uncomfortable Record]

One secret Israel lobby controls the governments of every Western country.

False, aimed the other way

The record shows several legally disclosed advocacy groups that work differently in each country, not one secret body in control. In the US, AIPAC is a registered lobby with a reported budget over $100 million [cite:wikipedia_aipac], and the largest pro-Israel group by membership is Christians United for Israel, an evangelical organization claiming over 10 million members [cite:wikipedia_cufi]. In Britain, Conservative Friends of Israel and Labour Friends of Israel work inside both parties, but unlike AIPAC they do not spend on elections [cite:greatrep_uk]. Germany's support rests mainly on a stated government doctrine tied to its historical responsibility for the Holocaust, not on a lobby.

The kernel of truth: these groups are real and sometimes cross lines. In 2017 an Israeli embassy official in London was filmed discussing how to "take down" a British minister, and he left his post [cite:mee_patel]. Mediapart reported in November 2025 that the Israeli government directly reimbursed the European group ELNET for a French Senate event [cite:mediapart_senate]. That is documented influence, not control of every Western government.

Read more [scene:arm_s07|Volume XXXIX, The Arms Supply Architecture: How This Relationship Gets Maintained Politically] · [scene:s19g|Volume VI, The Machine, Named: The Lobby Goes Global] (volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

Epstein was obviously running a Mossad operation.

Unsupported

No court record, released government document or sworn testimony shows that Epstein worked for Israeli intelligence. The claim rests mainly on an unconfirmed, second-hand remark attributed to Alexander Acosta and on Ari Ben-Menashe, a source with documented credibility problems; Israel denies it [cite:politico_acosta_epstein_2019] [cite:wiki_ari_ben_menashe]. An FBI informant document obtained through FOIA records an informant saying Epstein was an Israeli spy, but it documents what an informant told the FBI, not anything the FBI verified [cite:fbi_epstein_spy].

Some ties are real. Epstein and former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Barak jointly brokered Israeli surveillance technology to Côte d'Ivoire [cite:aljazeera_epstein_ivory_coast_2026]. Ghislaine Maxwell's father, Robert Maxwell, was buried in Jerusalem in 1991 with the honors of a state funeral, a documented fact about his own standing in Israel; books alleging he worked with Israeli intelligence rely heavily on Ari Ben-Menashe and secondary accounts, and a father's relationships are not evidence about what his daughter or Epstein did [cite:jta_maxwell_funeral_1991] [cite:wiki_robert_maxwell]. Roughly three million files remain withheld, so the question stays open, not proven [cite:efta_wiki_transparency_act].

Read more [scene:epn_s05|Volume XL, The Epstein Network Architecture: What Holds, What Doesn't, and Why the Slide Matters] · [scene:epx_s07|Volume XL, The Epstein Network Architecture: The Father] (volume in preparation; opens in the simulation for now)

chapters.label: Prelude
chapters.title: The Board Before the Game
chapters.intro:
On 27 July 1694 a royal charter created the Bank of England, a company through which 1,268 private subscribers had lent the English Crown £1.2 million at 8 percent to fight France. [cite:rs_rd0_boe_museum] Palestine, at that date, was a group of Ottoman districts, part of an empire that had governed the Arab Middle East without internal borders since 1516 and let its recognized religious communities run their own courts and schools. [cite:w_ottoman_millet] Its people were mostly Arabic-speaking Muslims and Christians, with long-established Jewish communities in Jerusalem, Hebron, Safed and Tiberias. No Zionist organization existed, and none would for two centuries. This volume begins its account there, in a City of London where finance already sat inside the legislature, and ends in 1896, the year Theodor Herzl published Der Judenstaat and was refused by the banker who was already paying for Jewish colonies in Palestine. [cite:herzl_judenstaat] [cite:herzl_diaries_vol2_archive]

The stage asks a single question: what actually existed, on the documentary record, before political Zionism did? That means finding out which states, lenders, churches, laws and communities could act on Palestine by 1896, by what instrument, and with what limits. It also means separating the record from the legends that have gathered around several of these institutions, some of them, like the story of Nathan Rothschild and Waterloo, antisemitic in origin. [cite:wiki_dairnvaell_satan_pamphlet]

The actors are many, and they did not act together. The sovereign was the Ottoman sultan: Abdülmecid I, who opened the reform era in 1839, and Abdul Hamid II, who suspended the first parliament in 1878 and whose government barred foreign Jews from settling and buying land in Palestine from 1882. [cite:rs_rd0_gulhane_wiki] [cite:rs_rd0_firstconst_wiki] [cite:rs_rd0_barin_2014] Egypt's Muhammad Ali and his son Ibrahim Pasha held the country from 1831 to 1840, until Britain, Austria, Prussia and Russia restored it to Istanbul. [cite:rs_rd0_oriental1840_wiki] Britain appears as a borrower, an empire guarding its route to India, and the home of an evangelical lobby led by Lord Shaftesbury; the United States, through its ministers at Constantinople and a petition signed by more than four hundred prominent Americans in 1891. [cite:rs_rd0_disraeli_1876] [cite:wiki_christian_zionism] [cite:rs_rd0_frus1888_may] The Rothschild houses and the papal bankers lent to states and to the Pope. On the Palestinian Arab side stand the rebels of 1834, Jerusalem's deputy Yusuf Diya al-Khalidi, the notables who protested against Jewish immigration in 1891 and the mufti Muhammad Tahir al-Husayni. [cite:rs_rd0_rood_1834] [cite:rs_rd0_khalidi_palquest] [cite:rs_rd0_antizionism_wiki] [cite:rs_rd0_beska_2007] On the Jewish side are the Old Yishuv of Jerusalem, the colonists of the First Aliyah and the first arrivals from Yemen, the writers and societies who turned a prayer into a program, the philanthropists Edmond de Rothschild and Maurice de Hirsch, and the Jews who opposed the whole idea, from Reform rabbis in Pittsburgh to the Orthodox community of Jerusalem. [cite:rs_rd0_barin_2014_pop] [cite:rs_rd0_firstaliyah_wiki] [cite:pittsburgh_platform_1885] [cite:rs_rd0_antizionism_wiki_dissent]

The sections follow that board roughly in time. They open with the City of London, the legend of three ruling enclaves, and the loan of 1694. They move to Europe between 1789 and 1815 and the rise of one Frankfurt banking family, then to Palestine between Napoleon's siege of Acre and the bombardment of 1840, through a revolt that historians still argue over. The London house's loans and the papacy's borrowing come next, then the Protestant restorationists of 1839 and 1891. Two Ottoman sections follow: the reform edicts and the parliament of 1877, then the Land Code of 1858 that required land titles to be registered. Then the Jewish story is traced from the religious debate over the Three Oaths, through the first rabbinic and secular programs and the Russian crisis of 1881–82, to the Jews already living in Palestine and the colonies founded from 1878. The Porte's restrictions and the first Arab protests are set beside each other, followed by Edmond de Rothschild's colonies, Hirsch's Argentine alternative, and the Dreyfus Affair that turned a Viennese journalist toward a state. The stage ends with [scene:bc_s07|the board as it stood in 1896].
chapters.outro:
By the end of 1896 nothing that would later make a Jewish state possible had yet been decided, but most of the ground on which it would be decided had been laid. It lay in layers, each built by different hands for purposes of their own, and almost none of them for Zionism.

The legal layer was Ottoman, and it was the firmest. Palestine was a set of imperial districts under a sultanate that had promised its subjects equality in 1839 and 1856 and granted a constitution in 1876, which Abdul Hamid II suspended, with its parliament, in February 1878. [cite:rs_rd0_gulhane_wiki] [cite:rs_rd0_reform1856_wiki] [cite:rs_rd0_firstconst_wiki] Two bodies of Ottoman law now pulled against each other. The Land Code and Tabu law of 1858 and the law on foreigners' property of 1867 had created a registered, saleable deed and placed a foreign owner "upon terms of equality with Ottoman subjects." [cite:wiki_ottoman_land_code_1858] [cite:rs_rd0_frus1898_law1867] The decisions and notes of 1882, 1888 and 1894 then tried to close that door to one group, ending with the bar of 27 March 1894 on land for Jewish immigrants "for political reasons." [cite:rs_rd0_barin_2014] [cite:rs_rd0_frus1888_may] [cite:rs_rd0_frus1898_angell] Above both stood treaties the Porte could not revoke alone: the Capitulations, and Article 62 of the Treaty of Berlin, which Britain cited against the land rules in 1893. [cite:rs_rd0_cojs_fo1893] Ottoman sovereignty over Palestine is settled. What remains contested is the character of the land laws, a loophole exploited on the reading of a Marmara thesis or a wider privatization on Kark's, and the date the land ban began, 1892, 1893 or 1894. [cite:rs_rd0_marmara_thesis] [cite:rs_rd0_kark_2017] [cite:rs_rd0_landpurchase_wiki_bans]

The administrative layer is where the law met the ground, and where it leaked. The governor of Jerusalem limited pilgrims' stays and, with a "Commission for Sale" chaired by the mufti, blocked sales in 1893. [cite:rs_rd0_cojs_moore1887] [cite:rs_rd0_beska_2007] Against him stood consuls who could take foreign Jews under their protection, as Britain had declared in 1847 it would for Jews whose own states did not, and ambassadors who called the pilgrim rule "ipso facto null and void" for British protégés. [cite:rs_rd0_barin_2014] [cite:rs_rd0_cojs_moore1887] By Barın's estimate more than 50,000 Jews settled despite the bans. [cite:rs_rd0_barin_2014] The Porte could issue rules; it could not enforce them against the treaty powers.

The institutional and financial layer was European and older than any of this. Since 1694 the British state had borrowed from private subscribers through a chartered company in the City, and the London Rothschild house had lent to Prussia in 1818, supplied the Bank of England in 1825 and advanced £4,000,000 for the Suez shares in 1875, which Disraeli defended as "a highway to our Indian Empire." [cite:rs_rd0_boe_museum] [cite:jwatte_rothschild_myths_record] [cite:rs_rd0_disraeli_1876] Each tie was a contract, and the legend of a family directing governments traces to an antisemitic pamphlet of 1846. [cite:wiki_dairnvaell_satan_pamphlet] The money that reached Palestine did not follow Herzl. Edmond de Rothschild's colonies, roughly thirty by one count and never totaled in any cited source, and Maurice de Hirsch's Jewish Colonization Association, £2,000,000 of authorized capital aimed first at Argentina, were both committed before 1896 to resettlement without a state. [cite:wiki_edmond_james_de_rothschild] [cite:hadassah_mag_hirsch] Herzl ended the year with a pamphlet, a "rude telegram" and no patron. [cite:herzl_diaries_vol2_archive]

The Palestinian Arab layer was a society with its own politics. It had risen in 1834 against conscription and disarmament and been crushed, and historians still divide over whether that revolt was a first stirring of national identity, as Kimmerling and Migdal hold, or a provincial rising for the Ottoman order, as Morris argues. [cite:rs_rd0_revolt1834_wiki] It had sent Yusuf Diya al-Khalidi to the parliament of 1877, where he opposed the Sultan until he was ordered out of Istanbul. [cite:rs_rd0_khalidi_palquest] Arab notables in Jerusalem asked the Grand Vizier on 24 June 1891 to bar Russian Jews and land sales, and in 1895 a Cairo editor accused the colonists of taking Arab livelihoods. [cite:rs_rd0_antizionism_wiki] [cite:rs_rd0_beska_2007] The strongest form of its case, on this record, was that a sovereign's own rules were being evaded through foreign protection, on land often registered in the names of absentee families rather than of those who farmed it. [cite:rs_rd0_landpurchase_wiki] Whether the earlier peasant clashes carried political meaning is disputed between a Jewish Agency overview and Beška. [cite:rs_rd0_jafi_opposition] [cite:rs_rd0_beska_2007]

The Jewish layer held a case of comparable force. Some 24,000 Jews lived in Palestine in 1880 by Barın's estimate, 13,900 of them in Jerusalem, on the eve of the First Aliyah; the movement that followed answered pogroms, the May Laws and a show trial in the first European state to emancipate its Jews. [cite:rs_rd0_barin_2014_pop] [cite:wiki_may_laws] [cite:wiki_dreyfus] Yet most Jews who fled Russia went to America, and Reform Judaism, Jellinek in Vienna and Jerusalem's Orthodox community all opposed the national idea. [cite:wiki_pogroms_russian_empire] [cite:pittsburgh_platform_1885] [cite:rs_rd0_antizionism_wiki_dissent]

The regional layer showed who decided. In 1840 Britain, Austria, Prussia and Russia, not the people of Palestine, returned the country to the Sultan, Britain seeking to "preserve Turkey" on the route to India. [cite:rs_rd0_oriental1840_wiki] [cite:rs_rd0_oriental1840_ellison] Egypt had held it for nine years; Yemen sent its first Jewish emigrants in 1881–82; Argentina offered land to Hirsch's colonists. [cite:rs_rd0_revolt1834_wiki] [cite:rs_rd0_firstaliyah_wiki] [cite:wiki_moises_ville]

The American layer was thin but already double. In 1888 Oscar Straus called passport rules tied to religion "utterly repugnant" to the Constitution, a defense of citizens' equality rather than of settlement; in 1891 the Blackstone Memorial, with more than four hundred signers, asked President Harrison to support a Jewish homeland. [cite:rs_rd0_frus1888_may] [cite:wiki_christian_zionism] The sources do not record Harrison's answer.

What was settled, then, was who held power: the Sultan held it in law, and the treaty powers held it in practice wherever their consuls reached. What was contested was nearly every reading of the period, from the revolt of 1834 to the land laws, the Porte's motives and the meaning of a single page of Herzl's diary. [cite:herzl_diaries] What the record leaves open is how the pieces would move once a political movement entered the game. The next stage begins with [scene:rd1_ottoman|the country Herzl's program was aimed at], and then at Basel in August 1897, with the congress he had resolved to convene instead of the patron he could not find.

sections.h: The Square Mile: Privilege Without Sovereignty
sections.html:
This volume opens not in Palestine, and not in any ministry or synagogue, but in a financial district of roughly one square mile in the middle of London. It is run by the oldest municipal corporation in Britain, the City of London Corporation. The Corporation governs through a Lord Mayor and a Court of Common Council, and it keeps its own police force. Its privileges predate Magna Carta, and when Parliament has legislated since, it has routinely preserved them by express exception written into the later Acts. [cite:wiki_city_of_london_corporation]

A claim widely repeated online holds that the City is a sovereign city-state, beyond the authority of Parliament and the Crown, and that the monarch must ask the Lord Mayor's permission before entering it. The documents do not bear that out. What they show is in some ways more instructive: three privileges that are real, unusual and on the record, and none of which amounts to statehood.

The business vote. In Corporation elections, businesses are allocated votes alongside the people who live there. At the City elections of April 2013, the roughly 9,000 resident votes were outnumbered by a business vote some 32,000 strong. Those figures come from the Green Party, which campaigns to end the arrangement, and they should be read as a campaigner's figures. The same Green Party statement cited a Bloomberg survey that questioned how far the business vote represented the workers it is supposed to speak for. [cite:greenparty_remembrancer_2013] [cite:wiki_city_of_london_corporation] The arrangement is unique in the United Kingdom. In practical terms it means that the firms based in the district, rather than its residents alone, choose much of its government.

The Remembrancer. The second privilege places the Corporation inside Parliament itself. The City Remembrancer is a Corporation official who may watch the House of Commons from the visitors' under-gallery, near the Serjeant at Arms, by the Speaker's permission rather than by right. A claim often repeated, that he is the only outsider allowed on the floor of the House, is not supported: he has no access beyond the bar. [cite:dv2_wiki_remembrancer] [cite:dv2_wanderer_remembrancer] The office reviews parliamentary legislation in order to protect the Corporation's interests, and it does so with a budget reported at about £6 million and a team of in-house lawyers. [cite:greenparty_remembrancer_2013] [cite:wiki_city_remembrancer] The author Nicholas Shaxson has called the office "the world's oldest institutional lobbyist." In 2013 the Green MP Caroline Lucas formally asked the Speaker to remove the Remembrancer from the floor of the House. [cite:greenparty_remembrancer_2013] [cite:ohuiginn_city_corporation] The sources used here record the request; they do not record what came of it.

This is the heart of the matter. A lobbyist ordinarily stands outside a legislature and seeks to be heard. The Remembrancer watches from inside one and reads bills as they pass with a single client's interests in mind. Read together, the business vote and the Remembrancer can be seen to reinforce each other: the firms help choose the Corporation, and the Corporation keeps watch on the law that governs them. Who could not act in the same way is equally plain. No other local authority, and no group of residents anywhere else in the country, has a comparable seat.

Temple Bar. The third privilege is ceremonial, and it is the one the legend rests on. When the monarch enters the City on a state occasion, the Lord Mayor meets the sovereign at Temple Bar and presents the City's sword. An account published in 1869 described the custom as the Mayor "requiring" the sovereign to ask leave to enter. [cite:wiki_temple_bar] The record shows a courtesy, not a legal requirement. The sovereign's carriage has passed Temple Bar without stopping, as the BBC's Huw Edwards noted on air during a Jubilee, and Parliament's authority over the City is a matter of statute, not of the Lord Mayor's leave. [cite:metabunk_city_sovereign_debunk] [cite:wiki_temple_bar]

Laid side by side, the claim and the record separate cleanly.

The test that matters is whether the City's privileges amount to sovereignty, and they do not. The Corporation is a local authority, not a state. It has less autonomy than the Crown Dependencies of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man, each of which has its own legislature. Parliament can legislate for the City, and does. [cite:metabunk_city_sovereign_debunk] [cite:ohuiginn_city_corporation] The privileges survive because Parliament keeps choosing to preserve them, which is the opposite of standing above Parliament.

The Corporation's own description of itself is more revealing than the legend. It has said that it acts "rather like a trade body" for finance and business. [cite:ohuiginn_city_corporation] That is the documented finding, and it is the more serious one, precisely because it is true. A sovereign enclave would be a curiosity of constitutional law. A trade body for finance with its own electorate of firms and an official seated in the Commons is a working arrangement of influence, open to examination, and examined here on those terms.

What the record leaves open should be said as plainly. The vote figures come from a party that wants the business vote abolished, and the Remembrancer's budget is a reported figure, not one drawn from published accounts in the sources used here. Nor do these sources measure how often the Remembrancer's work changed the text of a bill. The influence is structural and documented; its effect on any particular law is not established here.

That is why the story starts in the Square Mile. The City matters to this history not as a hidden sovereign but as something older and better documented: a long-standing arrangement by which finance held a formal place inside the legislature of the state that would later issue [scene:s06|the Balfour Declaration]. Its firms could vote, and its interests were read into bills before they passed. The banking houses that appear in the sections that follow did their business inside this structure.

sections.h: Three Enclaves and One Trope
sections.html:
The City of London is often bundled with two other capitals into a single story. In its most common form, the City of London, Vatican City and Washington, DC are three sovereign city-states that together and in secret govern the world's finance, its religion and its military. Each of the three is a real jurisdictional oddity, and each contains a real gap in ordinary accountability. The claim that they form one coordinated power is a different matter. The way to test it is to set out what the legal record shows about each enclave on its own terms, and then to ask what, if anything, connects them.

The City. As the previous section showed, the City of London Corporation is a local authority whose privileges are preserved by express exception in Acts of Parliament. It has an electorate that includes businesses, and an official lobbyist, the Remembrancer, who watches the Commons from its under-gallery. It is not a state. Parliament legislates for it, and the Crown Dependencies have more autonomy than it does. [cite:wiki_city_of_london_corporation] [cite:metabunk_city_sovereign_debunk] Its peculiarity is privilege without sovereignty.

Vatican City. The second enclave is the only one of the three that is in fact a sovereign state, and it became one late. Vatican City became sovereign on 11 February 1929, through the Lateran Treaty with Mussolini's Italy. The treaty recognized papal sovereignty over an enclave of 44 hectares, and Italy paid the Holy See compensation for the Papal States it had lost in 1870. [cite:wiki_lateran_treaty] Before 1929 there was no Vatican state in this sense, so the enclave cannot have been a sovereign partner in any arrangement reaching back into the period this volume covers. Its financial bodies, the IOR, APSA and the Governorate, publish no statements equivalent to those of a comparable secular institution, and they sit outside EU banking regulation. [cite:wiki_lateran_treaty] The treaty, the compensation and the financial bodies belong to later volumes of this library, which take them up in full. Here only the legal fact matters: sovereignty, from 1929, by treaty.

The District of Columbia. The third enclave is the reverse of a sovereign city. Washington, DC is a federal district under the exclusive legislative authority of Congress, under Article I, Section 8 of the United States Constitution. Its residents have elected a mayor and council only since the District of Columbia Home Rule Act of 1973, and Congress keeps a veto over the District's legislation. Its roughly 700,000 residents have no voting member in either house of Congress. [cite:wiki_dc_home_rule] Far from ruling anything, the capital has less self-government than any state of the Union. The 1973 Act, like the Lateran Treaty, belongs to a later period; it appears here only to fix what kind of place the District legally is.

Set side by side, the three show what is documented and what is not.

The last row is the one that decides the question. The "empire of three cities" assigns each enclave a portfolio: finance to London, religion to Rome, the military to Washington. For such an empire to exist, something would have to bind the three: a treaty, a charter, a shared council, or at the very least documented coordination between them. The record contains none of these. [cite:metabunk_city_sovereign_debunk] The three have different legal foundations, created centuries apart by different authorities. One is a medieval corporation kept alive by Parliament's exceptions. One is a sovereign created by a twentieth-century treaty with Italy. One is a federal district that its own Congress governs. The only thing they share is that each is an anomaly inside a capital.

The way the claim travels matters as much as its lack of a source. In circulation, the story reliably slides. It begins with three real jurisdictional oddities, moves on to an assertion about hidden rulers behind them, and from there passes into older ethnic and religious tropes about who those hidden rulers supposedly are. [cite:metabunk_city_sovereign_debunk] That last step is where the claim does its real work, and it is the step this library refuses. The three enclaves give no support to it; they are simply a container into which it has been poured. Where a later section of this volume meets real antisemitic material, such as hostility to the papal loans framed around the lenders' Jewishness, it names it as what it is. The "three cities" story belongs in the same category whenever it takes that final step.

None of this makes the three enclaves uninteresting. Each is a genuine carve-out from ordinary accountability: a franchise for business inside a national legislature, a sovereign's financial bodies outside EU banking regulation, a capital whose residents have no vote in the body that governs them. That is more than enough to examine, and later volumes do. What bundling them into one hidden empire adds is nothing the documents support, and everything they do not.

The gap here is narrow, and it should be stated exactly. The sources used here establish the legal status of each enclave and the absence of any documented link among them. They do not, and could not, prove a negative about every private contact among officials of three governments across centuries. What they do show is that the claim has no primary source behind it, and the burden of producing one rests with those who make it. Until such a document appears, the record supports three separate accountability gaps, each mapped on its own terms, and that is how this library treats them.

sections.h: 1694: The Bank, the War and the Debt
sections.html:
The City's privileges reach back past Magna Carta. The institution through which the British state learned to borrow is younger, and this volume's clock starts with it, in 1694, because of a loan. In that year a group of private subscribers lent the English Crown £1.2 million through a newly chartered company, and the company that held the loan became the Bank of England. The arrangement outlived the war it was raised for. This section reads it as the pattern by which a state at war could borrow large sums from private lenders on a regular footing, and as the structure into which the banking houses of the following sections would lend. To see why it was built, the story has to begin twenty-two years earlier, with a default.

On 2 January 1672 the government of Charles II began what became known as the Stop of the Exchequer. It suspended repayment of Exchequer orders and warrants, the instruments through which the Crown had borrowed. The Stop was planned to last one year. It was extended to May 1673, and then to January 1674. [cite:rs_rd0_stop_exchequer] The sums caught by it were large for the period. The obligations were later estimated at £1,211,065 by the historian Horsefield, and the principal was assessed at £1,328,526 at the end of 1676; both figures come here through a reference summary. The lenders who bore the loss were the goldsmith-bankers of London, and several were ruined. Edward Backwell and Robert Vyner were among those who went bankrupt. [cite:rs_rd0_stop_exchequer]

The Bank of England's own museum draws the line from that default to its founding. Because Charles II had failed to repay the goldsmiths, they were unwilling to lend to the Crown again. When William III needed money for his war against France, he had to find another lender. [cite:rs_rd0_boe_museum] This is the Bank's explanation of its own origins, offered by its museum, and it should be read as such. The Bank's 1970 booklet The Bank of England: History and Functions states the purpose in the same terms: the Bank was "incorporated by Act of Parliament and Charter in 1694" to help "finance the war being fought by William III against Louis XIV of France." [cite:rs_rd0_boe_hf1970]

The scheme came from a Scottish merchant, William Paterson. He proposed that members of the public lend the government £1.2 million, a sum the Bank itself puts at about £200 million in today's money. The subscription was raised in 11 days by 1,268 subscribers. [cite:rs_rd0_boe_museum] The Bank was formally established by Royal Charter on 27 July 1694. [cite:rs_rd0_boe_museum] [cite:rs_rd0_boe_hf1970] According to a reference summary of the national debt's history, which draws on H. Roseveare's The Financial Revolution 1660–1760 (1991), the charter was granted through the Tonnage Act 1694, and Sir John Houblon became the first governor. [cite:rs_rd0_natdebt_wiki] The new institution first did business in the Hall of the Mercers' Company in Cheapside. [cite:rs_rd0_boe_hf1970]

Who should be called the Bank's founder is a matter on which the sources place their emphasis differently. The Bank's museum credits the scheme to Paterson, who proposed that the public lend to the government. [cite:rs_rd0_boe_museum] The reference summary, citing Roseveare, credits Charles Montagu with devising the Bank's establishment, and notes that Paterson's plan had been put forward about three years earlier without being acted on. [cite:rs_rd0_natdebt_wiki] The two accounts are compatible rather than opposed: Paterson proposed, and Montagu carried the proposal through. A reader who meets either name presented as the sole founder is meeting half of the record.

The mechanism was simple, and its simplicity was its strength. The subscribers did not lend to the King as private individuals, as the goldsmiths had. They lent through a joint-stock company, "The Governor and the Company of the Bank of England," and became its shareholders. [cite:rs_rd0_boe_museum] The government paid them 8% interest on the loan. The Bank's museum sets that rate against what the goldsmiths had typically charged the Crown: 20 to 30%. [cite:rs_rd0_boe_museum] According to the reference summary, the government also paid a management charge of £4,000 a year on the loan. [cite:rs_rd0_natdebt_wiki] The lender's risk had been changed in kind. Instead of individual goldsmiths exposed to a royal default, as in 1672, the creditor was now a chartered corporation established by Act of Parliament and Charter, whose shares were held by its 1,268 subscribers. That changed who could lend to the state, and on what terms.

Who gained, and who bore the cost, can be stated only as far as these sources go. The Crown gained what it had lost in 1672: access to credit for war, at well under half the rates the goldsmiths had typically charged. The subscribers gained a steady 8% on their money and a share in a chartered company. The cost fell on the government's finances, which owed the interest and the management charge year after year. The sources used here do not say which revenues paid that interest or who, among the King's subjects, ultimately carried it, and this section does not guess.

What the Bank became is better documented than its founders' intentions. The 1970 booklet describes it as "banker to the Government" and as manager of "the Government Stocks which form the bulk of the National Debt." [cite:rs_rd0_boe_hf1970] It dates two later turning points: the Bank Act of 1844, which centralized the issue of banknotes in the Bank, and the Bank of England Act of 1946, which brought the Bank into public ownership. [cite:rs_rd0_boe_hf1970] Until 1946, then, the institution through which the British state borrowed and managed its debt was a privately owned company.

The debt that the Bank managed grew with each war. At the end of the Napoleonic Wars, British government debt reached a peak of about £1 billion, more than 200% of GDP. That figure is given by the reference summary, which takes it from the website ukpublicspending.co.uk, and it should be read as an estimate. [cite:rs_rd0_natdebt_wiki] The scale is the point. A loan of £1.2 million in 1694 had become, a little over a century later, part of a debt of about £1 billion, larger than the whole of a year's national output twice over.

That growth is what ties 1694 to the rest of this volume. A state that borrowed this way needed lenders who could raise large sums quickly, across borders, in wartime. The Napoleonic Wars, which pushed the debt to its peak, were also the years in which one Frankfurt family placed its sons in five capitals and became the most reliable creditor to governments that kept falling, as [scene:s01|the next section] shows. The London house that family founded would later lend to the British state directly, as [scene:bc_s02|the section on N M Rothschild & Sons] sets out. Neither house invented the system. Both lent into one that the Bank of England had organized more than a century before. The privileges of [scene:bc_s01|the City Corporation] and the borrowing machinery of the Bank are separate institutions in the sources used here, and this book keeps them separate.

Several things remain unsettled. The Stop's figures, the £4,000 management charge, the role of Montagu and the £1 billion peak all reach this book through reference summaries rather than the underlying scholarship, and they are given here as those summaries give them. The Bank's account of why it was founded is the Bank's own. The sources do not identify the 1,268 subscribers, so nothing here can say who they were, what trades they followed or how widely the shares were held after 1694.

sections.h: The Board Before the Game, 1789–1815
sections.html:
The Bank of England had given a state at war a way to borrow on a regular footing. The wars against revolutionary and Napoleonic France would test that machinery, and they would make the fortune of the lenders who could serve it. A common way of telling Israel's story begins with the Holocaust, as though nothing before it mattered. The record begins much earlier. The dynasties, states and religious institutions that would later fund the Zionist project, permit it or shape the ground it worked on were all in place by 1789, a full century before the political movement was founded. Between 1789 and 1815 the Napoleonic wars redrew the map of Europe. In those same years one Frankfurt family placed five sons in five capitals and, by 1815, had become the most reliable creditor to regimes that kept collapsing. This section sets out that board: the family first, then the states around it.

It is a subject on which two errors are common, and this section avoids both. The Rothschild dynasty is real, and its banking history is one of the best-studied cases of dynastic finance in modern European history. That same history has served for two centuries as the raw material for antisemitic conspiracy theory. Both facts are on the record, and the work of this section is to keep them apart.

Mayer Amschel Rothschild. The founder, Mayer Amschel Rothschild (1744–1812), was born in the Frankfurt Judengasse, the walled Jewish quarter where the law of the Holy Roman Empire required Frankfurt's Jews to live. The family name came from the red shield on the house sign of an earlier ancestor. In the 1760s he trained as a numismatist, a dealer in rare coins for aristocratic collectors. That trade was his entry into the economy of the German courts; he was not yet a banker. In 1769 he was appointed Hoffaktor, court factor, to Landgrave Wilhelm IX of Hesse-Kassel. The post was a regulated intermediary role: Jews were barred by law from most professions but could serve as financial agents to particular nobles. In 1770 he married Gutle Schnapper. They had ten surviving children, five sons and five daughters, and under German succession law only the sons could inherit and manage the business.

The decisive moment came in 1806. In the Napoleonic Wars, Landgrave Wilhelm fled the French and entrusted his fortune to Mayer Amschel. On one account, that custody was the operational moment of the family's rise. Mayer Amschel died in 1812. His will, held in the Rothschild Archive in London, instructed his five sons to work only among themselves, to share information across borders, and to arrange marriages within the extended family so as to hold the capital together. At his death he was not the wealthiest man in Europe. He left a family firm about the size of a mid-tier private bank: a man rising, not yet risen.

Five sons, five capitals. Between 1798 and 1812 Mayer Amschel placed his sons in five European cities. Amschel stayed in Frankfurt and ran the original house. Salomon went to Vienna and the Austrian court, Nathan to London, Carl to Naples and the Italian states, and James to Paris. [cite:schama_two_rothschilds] The sources behind this volume do not agree on when the two western houses were formally founded. One dates N M Rothschild & Sons in London to 1811 and another to 1809. The Paris house, de Rothschild Frères, is dated to 1817 in one account and to 1812 in others; the detailed account used here has James arrive in Paris in 1812 and dates the firm to 1817. The structure itself is not in doubt.

The dispersion was the innovation, and the mechanism is clear. Five branches in five capitals let information move across borders faster than through the state postal systems. They let capital move between currencies and interest rates. They spread political risk, since trouble in one country did not threaten the whole. And they let the family underwrite loans to sovereigns who were at war with each other. This five-city structure meant the family could move capital across borders faster than any state. [cite:schama_two_rothschilds] The family's coat of arms, five arrows held in a fist, commemorates the five branches.

The model was distinctive in its scale but not unique in kind. The Barings in Britain, the Fuggers in an earlier Germany, the Warburgs in Hamburg, the Bleichröders in Berlin and later the Morgans in America all worked on similar dynastic, cross-border lines. This is the documented history of a kind of finance, not a conspiracy.

The London house and the wars. Nathan Mayer Rothschild (1777–1836) established the London house. Through the nineteenth century it was a principal underwriter of British government bonds, and in 1875 it financed Britain's purchase of shares in the Suez Canal. [cite:schama_two_rothschilds] In the last campaign against Napoleon, Nathan financed the payment of British subsidies to Britain's allies, and Wellington's army was partly paid through Rothschild couriers carrying gold to Spain. On this book's reading, this is where the family's business met the state borrowing that the Bank of England had organized a century earlier: a government at war needed lenders who could move money quickly across a continent, and the five houses could.

The most famous story about Nathan, that he learned of Wellington's victory at Waterloo a day early, by carrier pigeon, and made a fortune on the London Stock Exchange, is the one the sources handle least consistently. They agree that its popular form is antisemitic in origin and disagree on where it began and whether Nathan had any real advantage; both versions, and the evidence for each, are set out in [scene:bc_s02|the section on the London house].

The Paris house. James Mayer Rothschild (1792–1868), the youngest son, was sent to Paris at about nineteen, following his father's death and his father's testamentary instruction. Between 1817 and 1848 he built de Rothschild Frères into the largest private bank in France, underwriting French government loans under both the Bourbon Restoration and the July Monarchy. From the 1830s to the 1850s he financed the Chemin de Fer du Nord, the northern French railway and one of the largest infrastructure projects of the age, where much of the Paris fortune came to be concentrated. When he died in 1868 his was the largest single Rothschild branch by capital. It was mainly an investment bank, lending to states and building infrastructure. The house passed to his sons, principally Alphonse and Gustave. His youngest son, Edmond, was 23, and inherited substantial capital but not the management of the bank. [cite:schama_two_rothschilds]

The peak, 1815–1875. Between 1815 and 1875 the Rothschild banks were arguably the largest private-capital institution in the world. They underwrote sovereign loans for Britain, France, Austria and several Italian states. Their business was to make such loans pay for both lender and borrower, which is what an investment bank still does. The Vienna, Paris and Italian branches financed early railway building across Europe. From the 1830s, under Pope Gregory XVI, the papacy borrowed from the Rothschilds more than once; the papal loans are told in full in a later section. How large was all this? On Niall Ferguson's figures, as reviews of his history report them, the combined capital of the houses was £9.5 million in 1852 and £34 million in 1874, after which it grew little. [cite:wa_skidelsky] [cite:wa_steinberg_lrb] That is very large for its day, but nothing like the "half of the world's wealth" of the legend; the size of the fortune, and how it was kept private, is the subject of a later section. The Rothschilds were the largest private bankers of the period, not the only ones, and significant rather than dominant.

The decline after 1901. The founding house did not last. The Frankfurt house, the mother house of the dynasty, closed in 1901, because Amschel's line had produced no male heirs to carry it on. By the time of the Balfour Declaration in 1917, the original branch had been closed for sixteen years. The account used here traces the decline to four causes: the spreading of capital among dozens of cousins of uneven talent by the third and fourth generations; the rise of joint-stock banking, which outcompeted private family banks; the rise of American banking, which moved the center of world finance to New York; and the two world wars. In 1938 the Nazis expropriated the property of the Austrian branch, which the same account says is documented in exhibits at the Nuremberg trials. In the words of that account, the Rothschilds were victims of the Holocaust, not its orchestrators. By 1945, the dynasty as a coherent cross-border banking force had come to an end. Descendants today run separate businesses, among them Rothschild & Co in Paris, RIT Capital in London and various family offices, none of them near the dynasty's nineteenth-century scale.

Two branches, two positions. The family's later role in the history of Palestine runs through particular people, and the record keeps them distinct. The Paris branch produced Edmond de Rothschild (1845–1934), who from the 1880s used a large personal fortune to fund agricultural settlements of the First Aliyah in Ottoman Palestine, among them Rishon LeZion, Zikhron Ya'akov and Rosh Pinna, while personally opposing Theodor Herzl and the political Zionist Congress. [cite:schama_two_rothschilds] His colonies, his administrators and his refusal of Herzl are told in [scene:bc_s04|the section on Edmond's colonies]. The London branch later produced Walter Rothschild (1868–1937), a zoologist who founded a natural-history museum at Tring and in 1917 was chosen as the addressee of the Balfour Declaration. He did not draft it: the letter was drafted by Weizmann, Sokolow and Sykes and signed by Balfour, the Foreign Secretary, as [scene:s06|the section on the Declaration] sets out. [cite:schama_two_rothschilds] One Rothschild funded settlements and opposed Herzl; another received a letter he had not written. Antisemitic conspiracy writing merges the two into a single "Rothschilds." The historical record keeps them apart.

The states. Around the family stood the powers whose decisions would matter far more. Britain, financed at scale by Nathan's house through the nineteenth century, would issue the Balfour Declaration in November 1917. It did so as an imperial and strategic move that served three British interests at once: securing the approaches to Suez, keeping Russia in the First World War, and bringing America into it. [cite:cohen_palestine_great_powers] A century separates the bond-financing from the Declaration, and the record does not show that the first caused the second; the decision of 1917 had its own, later, strategic logic.

France, post-revolutionary and then Napoleonic, was financed at scale by James Mayer's Paris house. It was also, in 1791, the first European state to grant Jews full legal citizenship, the model of nineteenth-century emancipation that Zionism would later argue had failed. In 1894 the same France produced the Dreyfus Affair, the false conviction of a Jewish army captain, Alfred Dreyfus, which persuaded the Viennese journalist Theodor Herzl that legal emancipation had not made Jews safe even in the most enlightened states of Europe. [cite:herzl_diaries] These are two separate facts about one country, decades apart. The record does not show any causal link between the Paris bank and the Dreyfus Affair, which had its own military and political causes, or that French antisemitism in 1894 was a reaction to Jewish banking. The affair is told in its own section later in this volume.

Imperial Russia was home to the largest Jewish population in Europe. The Pale of Settlement, created by Catherine the Great in 1791, confined most Russian Jews to the empire's western provinces. After Tsar Alexander II was assassinated in March 1881, waves of pogroms swept Ukraine and southern Russia. About two million Jewish emigrants left the Russian Empire between 1881 and 1914 (one account extends the window to 1924), and the great majority went to America, not Palestine. [cite:cohen_palestine_great_powers] Some did go to Palestine, and their settlements are part of this volume's story. But the main current of the emigration ran elsewhere, which complicates any account that treats the flight from the pogroms and Zionist settlement as one movement.

Palestine itself was Ottoman, as it had been since 1516 and would remain until 1917, more than four centuries. Under the millet system, Christian, Muslim and Jewish communities had substantial internal self-government. [cite:wiki_ottoman_palestine] The source behind this point adds that the Ottoman parliamentary reforms of 1876 brought Palestinian representation, and that Palestinian delegates sat in the Ottoman parliament. The parliamentary record gathered for a later section supports one such delegate: Yusuf Diya al-Khalidi, elected in 1877 as the sole deputy for Jerusalem. [cite:rs_rd0_khalidi_palquest] The plural is not supported beyond that. Even on the narrowest reading, a land under four centuries of continuous rule, with a working system of communal self-government, was not a blank space. How that order worked in Palestine from 1799 is the subject of the next section.

The last of the powers was the papacy. The Papal States were lost in 1870, and Vatican City became a sovereign state only in 1929, as an earlier section showed. The papacy's part in the later story of Israel arrives through absence: the Vatican did not recognize the State of Israel from its founding in 1948 until 30 December 1993, when the Vatican-Israel Fundamental Agreement was signed. [cite:jcpa_vatican_israel_recognition] As of 2026 that recognition remains in force, and it has survived public criticism from Rome, including the description of Gaza as an "ongoing massacre" by the Vatican Secretary of State, Cardinal Parolin, reported by the Times of Israel in October 2025. [cite:jcpa_vatican_israel_recognition] Why the Vatican waited 45 years is a question for later volumes.

A reading, not a finding. There is also an interpretation of what the family's history means for Palestine, for the region and for today. It is set apart here because it is a reading of the record, not part of the record. On that reading, the dynasty's direct role in Palestine ran through one branch only: one man, Edmond, in Paris, over four decades, 1882 to 1934. The Frankfurt house had no role in Palestine, and the London house had no part in funding it; Walter received a letter. The settlements Edmond paid for became part of the physical base of the Jewish community before the state, but the political order of the modern Middle East, from the Mandate to partition and the wars that followed, was made by states, not banking families. Ferguson, on this account, is explicit that the Rothschilds took part in some financial episodes and did not design the geopolitical order. To read the region as "Rothschild designed" is, on this reading, a category error that hides the documented actors: the British and American empires, the Israeli state, Palestinian resistance, the Arab states and Iran, intelligence services and arms makers.

The same account draws a lesson for the present. Dynastic finance still exists: it cites a 2024 Deloitte report counting about 15,000 family offices in the United States managing more than $6 trillion. Some of the families behind them are of Jewish origin and most are not. The "Rothschild" of modern conspiracy content, it argues, is an imagined dynasty that ceased to exist in coherent form between 1901 and 1945, not the businesses that carry the name today. The name survives in that content because it performs a substitution: it replaces an impersonal, documented pattern, concentrated capital passed down the generations, with a single Jewish family name. That turns a critique of a class into an ethnic one, and it lets the real pattern go unexamined. That is an interpretation, and it is labeled as one here.

What is documented, and what is refused. Stripped to the record, the history is this. Mayer Amschel Rothschild founded a banking family in Frankfurt in the late eighteenth century. His five sons went to five capitals. The family reached its peak in mid-nineteenth-century Europe as one of the largest private holders of capital in the world. The Frankfurt house closed in 1901, the Austrian branch's property was seized by the Nazis in 1938, and by 1945 the dynasty as a cross-border force was gone. Two framings are refused. The first holds that "the Rothschilds," as one undifferentiated collective, run world finance, started the world wars or engineered Israel. That claim is antisemitic in structure, because it puts a Jewish family name in place of the documented forces at work, and it is false on the evidence, since the family's businesses today are not large enough to do what the legend assigns them. The second is the defensive reply that the Rothschilds were "just another banking family" with nothing to examine. That evades a dynastic pattern that did shape European capital in the nineteenth century. The discipline is to name the family branch by branch and date each activity precisely. The account used here points readers to Ferguson's two-volume The House of Rothschild (1998–1999), to the Rothschild Archive, and to Simon Schama's Two Rothschilds and the Land of Israel (1978) for the distinction between the branches. [cite:schama_two_rothschilds]

Some of this remains unsettled. The founding dates of the London and Paris houses differ across the sources, as noted above, and the Waterloo story is told two ways. Several figures in this section, among them the capital estimate for 1875, the four causes of decline and the Nuremberg exhibits, reach this book through a single account summarizing Ferguson and the archive rather than through those works directly, and they are given here as that account gives them. The shape of the board in 1815 is clear enough: a Frankfurt family lending across five capitals, a British state borrowing on a scale the Bank of England had made possible, a France that had emancipated its Jews, a Russia that confined them, an Ottoman Empire that ruled Palestine, and a papacy that still held its own territory.

sections.h: Palestine in the Ottoman Order, 1799–1840
sections.html:
Of the powers on the board of 1815, the one that actually governed Palestine was the Ottoman Empire. Two opposite misconceptions are often told about Palestine before the twentieth century. One holds that the Middle East has always been a set of hostile nations locked in permanent war. The other comes in two forms that contradict each other: that the Ottomans "occupied" Palestine the way later settlers did, or that Palestine was an empty Ottoman backwater. The record supports none of these. For four centuries the land that this book follows was neither a nation among nations nor an empty space. It was a group of districts inside one large, multi-religious empire.

From 1516 to 1917 the Ottoman Empire governed most of the Arab Middle East as provinces of a single state, without international borders between them. Damascus, Baghdad, Jerusalem and Beirut were provincial cities of the same state, and people and goods moved among them without passports.
