On 30 December 2010 Benedict XVI established the Financial Information Authority (AIF) by motu proprio, as an institution connected to the Holy See. [cite:vt5_va_aif_profile] Francis widened its powers by a motu proprio of 8 August 2013 and Law XVIII of 8 October 2013, gave it new statutes on 15 November 2013, and gave it prudential supervision of financial activity, the IOR included. [cite:vt5_va_aif_profile] [cite:vt5_wiki_asif] On 5 December 2020 new statutes renamed it the Supervisory and Financial Information Authority (ASIF). [cite:vt5_wiki_asif] It was no rubber stamp in the eyes of its foreign counterparts either. After the Vatican Gendarmerie searched the offices of the Secretariat of State and of the AIF itself on 1 October 2019, in the inquiry into the London property deal, the Egmont Group of national financial intelligence units suspended the AIF on 13 November 2019, and lifted the suspension on 22 January 2020 only after the AIF gave assurances on the handling of shared intelligence, helped by a memorandum with the Vatican's Promoter of Justice. [cite:vt5_cwr_egmont2020] [scene:vt10_london_trial|Part Ten: the London trial]

The evaluations

The Holy See applied to MONEYVAL in 2011, after its first anti-money-laundering law. [cite:vt5_ncreg_aml2017] The first mutual evaluation report, adopted at MONEYVAL's plenary of 2 to 6 July 2012, rated 9 of the 16 core and key recommendations then in force compliant or largely compliant and 7 partially or non-compliant. [cite:vt5_mv_2012es] It found the AIF's role and independence unclear, noted that "no inspections have been undertaken" by it, and "strongly recommended that IOR is also supervised by a prudential supervisor"; it recorded that the 2010 law had been "wholly supplanted and replaced" by a decree of 25 January 2012, too recently for its effect to be assessed. [cite:vt5_mv_2012es] Progress reports followed in 2013, 2015 and 2017. The IOR's clean-up of its client files in this period closed about 4,600 accounts by the end of 2014 and about 4,800 by October 2015, and by late 2017 the AIF had sent 69 reports to the Promoter of Justice since 2013, none of which had yet reached a court. [cite:vt5_ncreg_aml2017] [cite:vt10_ansa_ior2015] [cite:vt10_ansa_aif2016] [scene:vt10_reform_aml|Part Ten: the account closures]

The second evaluation, after an on-site visit from 30 September to 13 October 2020, was adopted at MONEYVAL's plenary of 26 to 30 April 2021 and published in June. [cite:vt5_mv_2021mer] It rated the effectiveness of the system "substantial" in five of eleven areas and "moderate" in six, with none "low." [cite:vt5_mv_2021mer] [cite:vt5_or_barbagallo2021] Its criticisms were specific. The risk assessment underrated the threat from insiders at middle and senior level; the Promoter of Justice's office lacked staff for complex financial cases and investigations had been protracted; sanctions in money-laundering cases appeared minimal; and a large gap separated sums frozen or seized from sums confiscated. [cite:vt5_mv_2021mer] By the end of the visit there had been two convictions for laundering one's own proceeds, in 2018 and 2019, with a third on 21 January 2021, and confiscation orders of about 1.3 million euros. [cite:vt5_mv_2021mer] The standard on correspondent banking, the IOR's links to foreign banks, was rated non-compliant. [cite:vt5_mv_2021mer] The Holy See said it "welcomes the Moneyval Report" and "renews its commitment to continue working towards full compliance." [cite:vt5_pv_moneyval2021]

A follow-up report adopted at MONEYVAL's plenary of 20 to 24 May 2024 raised the correspondent-banking rating from non-compliant to compliant and two others, on wire transfers and on the transparency of legal persons, from partially to largely compliant. [cite:vt5_fatf_fur2024] [cite:vt5_pv_moneyval2024] The next assessment of technical compliance was set for about four years later, in MONEYVAL's sixth round. [cite:vt5_pv_moneyval2024] ASIF's report for 2024 recorded 79 suspicious-activity reports, down from 123 in 2023, and 11 referrals to the Promoter of Justice. [cite:vt5_ewtn_asif2025] No later MONEYVAL report on the Holy See was found as of October 2026.

What the checks reach

The financial checks reach further than the treaty bodies in one respect and less far in another. They reach further because they are tied to things the Vatican uses every day, the euro and its links to foreign banks; the 2012 warning on IOR supervision was followed within a year by prudential supervision, and the correspondent-banking rating was repaired by 2024. [cite:vt5_mv_2012es] [cite:vt5_fatf_fur2024] They reach less far because they test systems, not individual decisions: MONEYVAL rates laws, supervisors and prosecution records, and it was the Vatican's own prosecutors and tribunal, not the evaluators, who brought the London property case to trial. [cite:vt5_mv_2021mer] [scene:vt10_reform_aml|Part Ten: reform and anti-money-laundering] The record therefore corrects both the claim of exemption and the claim of no accountability, without supporting the opposite claim that the Vatican's money is now fully transparent; the evaluators' own findings on insider risk, prosecution and confiscation say otherwise.

sections.h: A Voice Without a Vote: The Soft-Power Thesis Tested
sections.html:
The previous sections asked why the Holy See is treated as a state and who checks it. This one asks what it does with that standing. The explainer channel Wendover Productions, in its video "How the Vatican's Embassies Work" (27 February 2025), argued three things: that the Holy See has soft power with no hard power behind it; that it tends to back winners, choosing "broadly reasonable positions" few will contest; and that it picks its battles, letting abortion "lie" at the international level. [cite:vt5_wendover] This section keeps that thesis as the video's argument and sets the documented record beside each example it uses.

The UN seat and why there is no vote

The video ties the UN seat to the Cuban Missile Crisis and to a visit by Secretary-General U Thant to the new pope, Paul VI. The visit is documented: Paul VI received U Thant on 11 July 1963 and called the United Nations "an instrument of brotherhood between nations." [cite:vt5_sp_pvi_uthant1963] On 21 March 1964 the Holy See notified U Thant that Mgr Alberto Giovannetti would be its first Permanent Observer, and the mission dates its status from 6 April 1964. [cite:vt5_sp_wiki_giovannetti] [cite:vt5_sp_hsm_history] The status rested on the Secretary-General's letter until resolution 58/314 of 1 July 2004 set out its rights, without a vote or candidates; the Holy See and the State of Palestine are the two non-member states with standing observer missions. [cite:vt5_sp_aleteia_un2024] [cite:vt5_hsm_58314] [cite:vt5_sp_ungeneva_nms] That the missile crisis won the seat is the video's narrative; the documents show the visit, the letter and the dates, not a motive. [scene:vt5_recognition|Why it is still treated as a state]

The video's reason for the missing vote is right in substance. Article 24 of the Lateran Treaty records the Holy See's wish to remain "extraneous" to temporal disputes between states and to congresses called to settle them, unless the parties jointly appeal to it, while reserving its moral authority. [cite:vt1_va_lateran] Cordell Hull cited Article 24 in 1944 when advising against Vatican membership, and Archbishop Celestino Migliore, a former observer, has said it has no vote "because this is our choice." [cite:dv1_wiki_holysee_un] The mission gives the reason as "absolute neutrality in specific political problems." [cite:vt5_sp_hsm_history]

John XXIII and the missile crisis

On 25 October 1962 John XXIII spoke on Vatican Radio in French, begging "all governments not to remain deaf to this cry of humanity"; Pravda carried the appeal the next day. [cite:vt5_sp_crux_jxxiii] According to the historian Norman Tanner, as reported by John L. Allen Jr., Kennedy reportedly used back channels to urge the pope to speak and Khrushchev later thanked him publicly; Tanner called the appeal a "factor" rather than a "crucial intervention." [cite:vt5_sp_crux_jxxiii] The video's account fits the record; any implication that it decided the outcome does not.

Cloning: the clearest win

On 7 August 2001 France and Germany asked for a convention against reproductive cloning. On 19 November 2001 Archbishop Renato Martino told the Legal Committee that "reproductive cloning is only part of the overall issue" and that creating embryos to be destroyed for stem cells must also be banned. [cite:vt5_sp_va_martino2001] A Belgian draft banned reproductive cloning and left other forms to states; a Costa Rican draft, with 44 other countries, banned all human cloning, a position the United States, Spain and the Philippines shared with the Holy See. [cite:vt5_sp_un_cloning2003] [cite:vt5_sp_wiki_multilateral] On 6 November 2003 the committee adopted Iran's motion, backed by 56 mostly Muslim states, to adjourn for two years, by 80 votes to 79 with 15 abstentions; the Assembly put the item back on its agenda on 9 December 2003. [cite:vt5_sp_un_cloning2003] [cite:vt5_sp_un_legal_cloning] On 8 March 2005 it adopted the non-binding United Nations Declaration on Human Cloning, resolution 59/280, by 84 to 34 with 37 abstentions, calling on states to prohibit all forms of cloning "incompatible with human dignity and the protection of human life"; the United Kingdom and China voted against. [cite:vt5_sp_un_ga10333] [cite:vt5_sp_un_news2005] The video's summary, that the text matched the view of a member that could not vote, is fair. "Backing winners" fits less well: the Holy See took the harder line early and the vote split.

Abortion: where the thesis is too strong

The video says the Holy See does not pursue abortion internationally. It does, at UN conferences. Before the Cairo population conference of September 1994, papal nuncios in about 60 countries lobbied for its positions, the Christian Science Monitor reported. [cite:vt5_sp_csm_cairo1994] On 13 September 1994 Archbishop Martino joined the consensus only "in an incomplete or partial manner", declining the health chapters, and said the Holy See "can therefore never condone abortion or policies which favor abortion." [cite:vt5_sp_ewtn_cairo1994] At Beijing it stated on 15 September 1995 that the outcome's family-planning language could not be read as endorsing methods it rejects, and the 2000 "See Change" campaign cited its record at conferences since Beijing in seeking to downgrade its seat. [cite:vt5_sp_wiki_multilateral] [cite:vt5_un_seechange2000] In April 2019 Archbishop Bernardito Auza said reading a right to abortion into reproductive health "explicitly violates the language of the ICPD." [cite:vt5_sp_cwr_auza2019] The record supports a narrower claim: the Holy See works openly to keep abortion out of consensus texts or to qualify them, rather than sponsoring texts of its own.

Cuba: credit shared

On 17 December 2014 the Secretariat of State said Francis had written to Raúl Castro and Barack Obama about humanitarian questions, including prisoners, and had received delegations of both countries "last October." [cite:vt5_sp_am_cuba2014] Obama said that day, "I want to thank His Holiness Pope Francis", citing his personal appeal on the American contractor Alan Gross, and credited Canada with hosting the talks. [cite:vt5_sp_wh_cuba2014] The video says the Cuban embassy reopened on 17 December 2014; that was the announcement, and embassies reopened on 20 July 2015. [cite:vt5_sp_aje_embassies2015] On 10 May 2015, after meeting Francis, Castro said: "I thanked the pope for what he did." [cite:vt5_sp_ap_castro2015]

The video's 2025 example is right in substance but rounds the number down to 500. On 14 January 2025 the White House said it would remove Cuba from the list of state sponsors of terrorism "as part of an understanding with the Catholic Church", Cuba said it would free 553 prisoners in the spirit of the Jubilee, and Cardinal Seán O'Malley said he had carried Francis's messages to both presidents for years. [cite:vt5_sp_ncr_cuba2025] Donald Trump restored the designation on taking office on 20 January. [cite:vt5_sp_cbs_trump2025] Cuba still announced on 10 March 2025 that all 553 were free; it called them people "sanctioned for diverse crimes", and rights groups said some appeared to be ordinary offenders. [cite:vt5_sp_aje_cuba2025] [cite:vt5_sp_cna_cuba2025] The Holy See secured a release; it could not hold the American side of the bargain.

Syria and Indonesia: presence, not leverage

The Holy See and Syria established relations on 21 February 1953; the Damascus nunciature stayed open through the civil war, and when Francis made the nuncio, Mario Zenari, a cardinal in October 2016 he kept him in post. [cite:vt5_sp_wiki_syria] [cite:vt5_sp_cns_zenari2016] The video's claims that Syrian officials sought papal mediation in 2000 could not be confirmed and are not repeated. In Indonesia the Holy See sent a delegate in 1947 and recognised the republic on 4 January 1950. [cite:vt5_sp_nunc_indonesia] Francis visited from 3 to 6 September 2024 and signed the Istiqlal Declaration on 5 September. [cite:vt5_sp_wiki_indonesia2024] The video presented the visit as a source of hope on church permits; the US Commission on International Religious Freedom reported in 2025 that the 2006 joint decree on houses of worship was still used against minorities, that churches were sealed or services halted in 2024, and that one Catholic parish had waited more than two decades to build. [cite:vt5_sp_uscirf_indonesia2025]

The video also garbles the city's area, which the Governorate gives as 0.44 km², about 0.17 square miles; it counts 117 nunciatures where I.Media, reporting the January 2026 note, counted 128; its 16 dicasteries match Praedicate Evangelium. [cite:vt4_vcs_geography] [cite:vt13_aleteia_dipl2026] [cite:vt6_va_pe] [scene:vt13_appointments_nuncios|Part Thirteen: nunciatures] Against the record, the thesis survives in a narrower form. The Holy See's tools are words, presence and the trust of parties who will not talk to each other; when a stronger party reverses course, as the United States did on Cuba, it has nothing to enforce with. The same limit governs its response to Gaza, where it has protested in strong terms and kept relations with Israel. [scene:vt18_why_no_sever|Part Eighteen: why relations were not severed] Where the video says it avoids hard fights, Cairo and Beijing show that it chooses them on doctrine, openly.

chapters.label: Part Six
chapters.title: Popes, Curia and the Myth of Hidden Popes
chapters.intro: Part Six turns from the Holy See's outside relations to the people who run it and to the stories told about who really does. It sets out how a pope is chosen under canon law and the conclave rules, using the conclave of May 2025 that elected Leo XIV, and how the Roman Curia has been organised since Francis's constitution Praedicate Evangelium of 2022: the Secretariat of State, the sixteen dicasteries, the economic bodies, and who holds the main offices as of October 2026. It then examines the "Black Pope", the nickname for the Superior General of the Jesuits: where the name comes from, what the office controls, who holds it now, and what happened when popes and Jesuit generals disagreed. It ends with the "Grey Pope", the claim of a hidden ruler above both, traced to its sources and graded, and with the documented answer to the question underneath all three: who decides.
chapters.outro: Part Six established that the chain of command in the Holy See is written down and has a single top. Canon law gives the pope supreme, full and immediate power with no appeal from his decree, and the cardinals under 80 choose each pope by a two-thirds secret ballot, as they chose Leo XIV on the fourth ballot on 8 May 2025. [cite:vt6_cic_331] [cite:vt6_wiki_conclave2025] The Curia as reorganised on 19 March 2022 works in his name through offices whose heads he appoints for five years and who lose office when he dies; as of October 2026 Cardinal Parolin remained Secretary of State, Archbishop Rudelli had become Substitute, and economic oversight sat with the Secretariat for the Economy under Maximino Caballero Ledo. [cite:vt6_ewtn_pe] [cite:vt6_va_parolin2026] [cite:vt6_vn_rudelli] [cite:vt6_gc_spe] The "Black Pope" is a nickname for the Jesuit Superior General, Arturo Sosa Abascal as of October 2026, who governs one religious order bound to the pope by a vow of obedience; when the two disagreed, in 1773 and 1981, the pope prevailed. [cite:vt6_wiki_supgen] [cite:vt6_gt_sosa2026] [cite:vt6_wiki_suppression] [cite:vt6_wiki_dezza] The "Grey Pope" has no office, no consistent holder and no document behind it, and is graded a myth. [cite:vt6_wiki_eminence] [cite:vt6_kettner_pepe] [cite:vt6_wiki_princeasst] Part Seven examines the family most often named as the hidden power, the Orsini, and the Roman "Black Nobility" to which it belonged. [scene:vt7_black_nobility|Part Seven: the Black Nobility]

sections.h: The Pope, the Conclave and the Curia since 2022
sections.html:
The question this part answers is the one most often asked about Rome: who actually decides. The answer begins with what the law says, because the Holy See is unusual in having written its chain of command down. Canon 331 of the Code of Canon Law of 1983 describes the Roman Pontiff as head of the college of bishops holding "supreme, full, immediate, and universal ordinary power" in the Church, and canon 333 adds that "no appeal or recourse is permitted against a sentence or decree of the Roman Pontiff." [cite:vt6_cic_331] In Vatican City State the same person holds the fullness of legislative, executive and judicial power under the Fundamental Law, most recently reissued by Leo XIV on 31 July 2026; that text and its delegations are set out in [scene:vt4_fundamental_law|Part Four]. [cite:vt4_vn_fl2026] This section follows the power from the moment a pope is chosen to the offices that work in his name.

How a pope is chosen

The cardinals form a college whose first legal task is to elect the pope; otherwise they assist him, collectively when he convokes them or individually through the offices they hold. [cite:vt6_cic_331] When the See falls vacant, the College governs only for ordinary or urgent business and to prepare the election. The Camerlengo, in 2025 Cardinal Kevin Farrell, administers the temporal goods of the Holy See; the heads of the curial departments lose office, with a few named exceptions such as the Major Penitentiary. [cite:vt6_vn_sedevacante] The rules of the election are those of John Paul II's constitution Universi Dominici Gregis (1996) as amended: only cardinals under 80 on the day the vacancy begins may vote, the constitution caps the electors at 120, voting is by secret ballot in the Sistine Chapel, and election needs two-thirds of the electors present, a rule Benedict XVI restored in 2007 and confirmed in 2013. [cite:vt6_vn_sedevacante]

The last application of these rules is recent and well documented. Francis died on 21 April 2025. The conclave opened on 7 May 2025 with 133 of the 135 eligible electors; two stayed away for health reasons. The two-thirds threshold was set at 89 votes, Cardinal Pietro Parolin presided as the senior elector, and on 8 May 2025, on the fourth ballot, the cardinals elected Robert Francis Prevost, who took the name Leo XIV and was inaugurated on 18 May. [cite:vt6_wiki_conclave2025] Born in Chicago on 14 September 1955, he is an Augustinian friar, a former Prior General of his order, bishop of Chiclayo in Peru from 2015, Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops from 30 January 2023 and a cardinal from 30 September 2023; the Holy See describes him as the first Augustinian pope. [cite:vt6_vn_leobio] His previous post matters for this part: the office that screens every candidate for bishop was the one he ran before the conclave.

The electorate that will choose his successor is also on the record. As of May 2026 Leo XIV had not created any cardinals; 119 were of voting age, just under the 120 limit that his two predecessors had exceeded, and 29 would pass 80 within three years. [cite:vt6_aleteia_firstyear] He used the College instead as a consultative body, calling consistories for discussion on 7–8 January and 31 May 2026 at which no cardinals were created. [cite:vt6_ncr_consistory] No later creation of cardinals was found in the reporting checked for this volume; the count is given as of May 2026.

The Curia after Praedicate Evangelium

The Roman Curia is the set of offices through which the pope governs the Church. Canon 360 says it acts "in his name and by his authority." [cite:vt6_cic_331] Its present shape was set by Francis's apostolic constitution Praedicate Evangelium, promulgated on 19 March 2022 and in force from Pentecost, 5 June 2022, which replaced John Paul II's Pastor bonus of 1988. [cite:vt6_vn_pe] The constitution groups the Curia into the Secretariat of State, sixteen dicasteries and a set of economic and judicial bodies. The dicasteries run from Evangelization and the Doctrine of the Faith through Bishops, Clergy and Consecrated Life to Legislative Texts and Communication. [cite:vt6_va_pe] The first of them, the Dicastery for Evangelization, "is presided over directly by the Roman Pontiff", with two pro-prefects doing the daily work. [cite:vt6_vn_pe]

Three general rules in the constitution bear on who decides. First, any member of the faithful, lay man or woman included, can head a dicastery, because the authority exercised there is the pope's, received from him. Second, prefects and members are appointed for five-year terms. Third, when the See is vacant "all heads of curial institutions and members cease from their office," except the Major Penitentiary and the Almoner. [cite:vt6_ewtn_pe] Curial power is therefore delegated, time-limited and personal to the pope who granted it; it does not survive him as an independent authority.

At the centre sits the Secretariat of State, which the constitution calls "the Papal Secretariat" providing "close assistance to the Roman Pontiff." It has three sections: General Affairs, headed by the Substitute, which handles the pope's daily business and coordinates the dicasteries; Relations with States and International Organizations, the foreign ministry; and Diplomatic Personnel. [cite:vt6_ewtn_pe] The Holy See's dealings with Israel and Palestine in later parts run through this office.

The money offices

Before 2020 the Secretariat of State also managed large funds of its own. By a motu proprio of 26 December 2020, in force on 1 January 2021, Francis moved the management of its investments, property and bank holdings, including the administration of Peter's Pence, to the Administration of the Patrimony of the Apostolic See (APSA), under the oversight of the Secretariat for the Economy; he had announced the decision to Parolin by letter in August 2020. [cite:vt6_vn_apsa2020] The investment that preceded the change, the London property, is examined in [scene:vt10_london_trial|Part Ten]. Praedicate Evangelium then fixed the economic structure: a Council for the Economy, the Secretariat for the Economy, APSA, an Auditor General, a Commission for Confidential Matters and a Committee for Investments. [cite:vt6_va_pe] The Secretariat for the Economy "functions as a Papal Secretariat for economic and financial matters": it supervises the administration of curial bodies and Peter's Pence, prepares the annual budget and the consolidated balance sheet of the Holy See, and must consult the Council for the Economy. [cite:vt6_va_spe] Founded on 24 February 2014, it was headed by Cardinal George Pell to 2019, Fr Juan Antonio Guerrero Alves to 2022 and, since 1 December 2022, by a layman, Maximino Caballero Ledo. [cite:vt6_gc_spe] How these bodies hold and spend money is the subject of [scene:vt9_apsa_governorate|Part Nine].

Who holds which office, October 2026

Leo XIV has changed personnel slowly. He kept Parolin as Secretary of State and Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández at the Doctrine of the Faith, named Archbishop Filippo Iannone to his own former dicastery in September 2025, and told the Curia on 24 May 2025 that "popes pass, the Curia remains." [cite:vt6_aleteia_appts] On 30 March 2026 he made Archbishop Paolo Rudelli Substitute in place of Archbishop Edgar Peña Parra, who became nuncio to Italy. [cite:vt6_vn_rudelli] Parolin was still signing as Secretary of State on 26 September and 1 October 2026. [cite:vt6_va_parolin2026] The Governorate of the city has been headed since 1 March 2025 by Sister Raffaella Petrini, the first woman in the post, whom Leo XIV confirmed on 9 May 2025. [cite:vt6_vn_petrini] [cite:vt6_wiki_petrini]

How a decision moves

The clearest way to see the division of labour is to follow one routine decision, the appointment of a bishop, through the offices. Bishops of a region propose names; the nuncio investigates the candidates and the diocese and sends three names, the terna, with his preference to the Dicastery for Bishops; the dicastery discusses and votes, and may accept the nuncio's choice, pick another name or ask for a new list; its prefect presents the result to the pope, usually at a Saturday audience; the pope decides; the nuncio asks the candidate; the appointment is announced. The process often takes six to eight months. [cite:vt6_usccb_bishops] The pope signs, but by the time a file reaches him the nuncio and the dicastery have shaped which names he sees. That is the practical form of the answer this part gives in [scene:vt6_grey_pope_myth|its last section]: the decision is the pope's in law, and the offices that frame it are named, appointed by him and removable by him.

sections.h: The "Black Pope": a Nickname and an Office
sections.html:
Much writing about hidden power in Rome starts from a phrase: the "Black Pope". In that writing the head of the Jesuits is the real ruler and the pope in white is his front. A milder version describes "White Pope and Black Pope offices", with the Jesuit general as the layer that implements the Vatican's decisions; the institutional role it implies does not survive a check against the record. This section sets out where the nickname comes from, what the office it refers to actually controls, who holds it as of October 2026, and what the record shows when the two "popes" have disagreed.

Where the nickname comes from

"Black Pope" is not a title in any document of the Society of Jesus or the Holy See. It is an informal name for the Superior General of the Jesuits, most likely taken from the plain black cassock of the order against the white of the pope, and it may also reflect the fear of Jesuit influence in Protestant Europe in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. [cite:vt6_wiki_supgen] The Catholic apologetics organisation Catholic Answers describes it as a Roman joke from the period when the Jesuits were the most prominent missionary order, treating their head as a second pope, and calls conspiracy readings of it a "garbled understanding of a Catholic in-joke." [cite:vt6_ca_blackpope] That is the Catholic side's own account of the name; the documentary point it rests on, that the Superior General has no office in the government of the Holy See, is tested below against the constitution of the Curia and against the record.

The conspiratorial reading has its own documented history. The Southern Poverty Law Center traced one prominent modern version, Eric Jon Phelps's "Vatican Assassins", to centuries of Protestant anti-Jesuit writing and to the nativist Know Nothings and American Protective Association, whose texts Phelps reissued. In his version the Jesuits rule the world "directly or through their Jewish and Masonic proxies"; the SPLC classed the site as a hate site. [cite:vt6_splc_phelps] The two prejudices are joined in that sentence. A theory that begins as a story about Catholics ends by naming Jews as the hidden instruments. This volume treats neither as evidence.

What the office controls

The Superior General governs one religious order. He is elected by the General Congregation, a gathering of Jesuit delegates that the order calls "the highest authority in the Society of Jesus" and that meets when the generalship falls vacant through death or resignation, or when circumstances require. [cite:vt6_wiki_gc] He is elected for life, as popes are, though the last three generals before the present one, Pedro Arrupe, Peter-Hans Kolvenbach and Adolfo Nicolás, resigned. He holds "governing power over all the members of the Society," which he normally exercises through the provincial superiors he appoints. [cite:vt6_wiki_supgen] His authority comes from the vows of Jesuits and ends with them: it reaches about a religious order and its works, such as schools and universities (examined in [scene:vt8_jesuits|Part Eight]), and no further.

The order's own law places it under the pope, not beside him. The founding Formula of the Institute defines the Society's purpose as serving "the Church, his spouse, under the Roman Pontiff." The professed members take a fourth vow of special obedience to the pope, whose "entire purport," the 35th General Congregation restated in 2008, "was and is with regard to missions": through it "the whole body of the Society puts itself at the disposition of the ministry of the Successor of Peter." [cite:vt6_gc35_d4] The Superior General holds no post in the Secretariat of State and heads no dicastery. The constitution of 2022 lists the Curia's offices in full, and the generalship of a religious order is not among them; the office holders as of October 2026 are set out in [scene:vt6_curia_2022|the previous section]. [cite:vt6_va_pe] [cite:vt6_gc_curia]

When the two "popes" disagreed

If the Superior General controlled the pope, the record of their conflicts would show it. It shows the reverse. On 21 July 1773 Clement XIV suppressed the Society throughout the world by the brief Dominus ac Redemptor: "We abolish and suppress the oft-mentioned Society." [cite:vt6_wiki_suppression] The Superior General of the day, Lorenzo Ricci, was imprisoned in the papal fortress of Castel Sant'Angelo and died there on 24 November 1775, having protested that the Society had given no grounds for its suppression. [cite:vt6_wiki_ricci] The order existed again only because a later pope, Pius VII, restored it in 1814. [cite:vt6_wiki_suppression]

The same pattern recurred in living memory. After Pedro Arrupe suffered a stroke in 1981, the Jesuits expected Vincent O'Keefe, the vicar general Arrupe had named, to lead them until a General Congregation could meet. In October 1981 John Paul II intervened and appointed his own delegate, Paolo Dezza, to govern the order in the interim; the Jesuits elected a new general, Peter-Hans Kolvenbach, only at the 33rd General Congregation in 1983. [cite:vt6_wiki_dezza] In both episodes the decision ran from the pope to the Jesuit general and was enforced against him.

Who holds it, October 2026

The present Superior General is Arturo Sosa Abascal, a Venezuelan Jesuit elected the 31st general by the 36th General Congregation on 14 October 2016, in succession to Adolfo Nicolás, who had resigned. [cite:vt6_je_sosa] He is the first Latin American in the post. As of October 2026 he remained in office: he made a visitation of a United States province from 26 January to 12 February 2026, and a Ghanaian newspaper reported on 12 October 2026 his visit to Ghana from 12 to 15 October, in the tenth anniversary year of his election. [cite:vt6_slu_sosa2026] [cite:vt6_gt_sosa2026] No convocation of a 37th General Congregation, which would be needed to elect a successor, was found in the sources checked for this volume; the reference list of congregations ends with the 36th in 2016. [cite:vt6_wiki_gc] His public role is visible and documented: visitations, letters to the order, meetings with provinces. Nothing in that record places him in the chain of decision of the Holy See.

The Society's own position, stated by its General Congregation, is that its distinctive bond is one of obedience to the pope for mission. [cite:vt6_gc35_d4] The conspiratorial position is that this obedience is a cover. That claim cannot be tested by any document, because it treats every document of obedience as part of the cover. The record that can be tested, suppression, imprisonment, restoration by papal act and papal intervention in the order's government, runs one way. The nickname survives because two men in Rome wear different colours. The authority runs from the pope to the general and not the other way. The coloured-pope scheme also has a third colour added on the internet, the "Grey Pope"; the next section takes it on its own terms.

sections.h: The "Grey Pope" and the Question of Who Decides
sections.html:
The fullest version of the hidden-pope story has three colours. The pope in white is the public face; the "Black Pope", the Jesuit general, runs the machinery; above both stands a "Grey Pope", usually said to be the head of the Orsini family or of the Roman "Black Nobility", sometimes a senior cardinal, who controls the other two and the money. This section describes the white, black and grey scheme only as a named claim. It traces where the parts of the claim come from, sets out what documents exist, grades the result and then gives the documented answer to the question underneath it: who decides in the Holy See.

Three colours that are documented, and one that is not

Rome does have colour nicknames, and they are on the record. The pope wears white. The Jesuit general is called the "Black Pope" after his order's cassock, as the [scene:vt6_black_pope|previous section] showed. [cite:vt6_wiki_supgen] There is also a "Red Pope": journalists long gave that name to the prefect of the Congregation for the Evangelization of Peoples, the old Propaganda Fide, in allusion to a cardinal's red and to his "almost absolute authority over mission territories." [cite:vt6_philstar_redpope] A 2023 academic biography of Cardinal Willem van Rossum, who ran the mission department in the early twentieth century, carries the nickname as its title. [cite:vt6_rup_redpope] Since 2022 that office has been held by the pope himself: under Praedicate Evangelium the new Dicastery for Evangelization "is presided over directly by the Roman Pontiff." [cite:vt6_vn_pe] Each of these nicknames attaches to a named office with a known holder.

Grey has a different origin, and it is not Roman. Éminence grise, "grey eminence", was the name given at the French court to Père Joseph, François Leclerc du Tremblay, a Capuchin friar in a grey habit who served as right-hand man to Cardinal Richelieu, the "red eminence". From him the phrase came to mean "a powerful decision-maker or advisor who operates covertly in a non-public or unofficial capacity." [cite:vt6_wiki_eminence] The phrase describes a type of adviser; it has never been the name of an office at the Holy See.

The claim chain

The "Grey Pope" in the form that circulates today is a recent internet construction, and its sources can be listed. A German bullion dealer's news page of 26 February 2024 calls "Pepe Orsini" the "grey pope", "chief of the Rothschilds, of the Rockefellers" and of the whole black nobility; it cites no source and concedes that reliable evidence for such power is scarce. [cite:vt6_kettner_pepe] An undated, unattributed web page calls "Pepe Orsini" "the ultimate, unelected power behind the Vatican", then states that no such person holds any official capacity and that the widely shared photograph may show an actor. [cite:vt6_sl_greypope] A third undated page gives the same title to a different man, the Jesuit Superior General, calls it "not an official title recognized by the Vatican" and cites only Aldous Huxley's biography of Père Joseph. [cite:vt6_woc_greypope] None of the three names a document. They do not agree on who the Grey Pope is. Two of them say there is no evidence for him.

The Orsini thread of the claim leans on a real family and a real, ceremonial post. The heads of the Orsini held the hereditary lay title of Prince Assistant to the Papal Throne from 1735 until January 1958, when Pius XII relieved Filippo Orsini of it after a public scandal; Paul VI's reform of the papal household in 1968 ended the title's hereditary character, and it is not now in use. [cite:vt6_wiki_princeasst] The family's documented record, and the claims made about it, are set out in [scene:vt7_orsini_record|Part Seven] and [scene:vt7_prince_assistant_1958|the removal of 1958]. The last formal link between the Orsini and the papal court was cut by a pope, against the family.

The Rothschild link in the 2024 version belongs to a much older line of story. Claims that the Rothschild family stands behind thrones and popes go back to anonymous pamphleteers of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. The journalist Mike Rothschild, who is not related to the family, has traced them as some two hundred years of antisemitic conspiracy theory. [cite:vt6_pw_rothschild] Folding the Rothschilds, the Rockefellers and a Roman prince into one hidden ruler repeats that story with a Catholic setting. The documented money between the Rothschild houses and Rome, papal loans from the 1830s on which the money ran from the bankers to the pope, is examined in [scene:vt11_papal_loans|Part Eleven], and the alleged unbroken chain to 2026 in [scene:vt11_chain_tested|the chain tested].

The grade

A claim of hidden office can be tested in three ways: is there an office, is there a holder, is there a document. The Holy See's offices are listed in full in its constitution of 2022 and in the Code of Canon Law, and no office stands above the pope; canon 333 rules out any appeal from his decree. [cite:vt6_va_pe] [cite:vt6_cic_331] No holder is identified consistently even by the pages that spread the claim, and one of them says the photograph shared as "Pepe Orsini" may show an actor. [cite:vt6_sl_greypope] [cite:vt6_woc_greypope] No document is cited by any of them. The broader idea of a hereditary nobility ruling through secret committees comes from conspiracy books such as John Coleman's Conspirators' Hierarchy (1992), for which fact-checkers have found no credible evidence. [cite:vt7_md_c300] A claim with no office, no holder and no document, contradicted by the documented acts of popes against the Orsini and the Jesuits, is graded a myth. The "Grey Pope" is a myth.

Who really decides

The documented answer is less dramatic and more definite. In law the pope decides: canon 331 gives him supreme, full, immediate and universal power, the Fundamental Law gives him the fullness of legislative, executive and judicial power in Vatican City, and the Curia acts "in his name and by his authority." [cite:vt6_cic_331] [cite:vt4_vn_fl2026] In practice he decides among options others prepare. The nuncio and the Dicastery for Bishops choose which three names he sees; the Secretariat of State drafts his documents and runs his diplomacy; the Secretariat for the Economy prepares his budget. [cite:vt6_usccb_bishops] [cite:vt6_ewtn_pe] [cite:vt6_va_spe] Every one of those office holders is named, appointed by him for five years and removable by him, and all of them lose office when he dies. [cite:vt6_ewtn_pe] Between popes, the cardinals under 80 decide who the next one will be, by a two-thirds secret ballot. [cite:vt6_vn_sedevacante]

The record also shows popes using that power against the bodies that hidden-pope stories place above them. Clement XIV suppressed the Jesuits, Pius XII removed the Orsini prince from his court post, John Paul II set aside the Jesuits' own interim leader, and Francis took the Secretariat of State's funds away from it in 2020. [cite:vt6_wiki_suppression] [cite:vt6_wiki_princeasst] [cite:vt6_wiki_dezza] [cite:vt6_vn_apsa2020] The limits on papal power are real, but they are visible ones: canon law and the structures his predecessors built, a Curia whose staff carries over ("popes pass, the Curia remains", in Leo XIV's words), finances that must balance, and outside checks such as the MONEYVAL evaluations described in [scene:vt5_moneyval_euro|Part Five]. [cite:vt6_aleteia_appts] [cite:vt5_mv_2021mer] Who holds those offices, and what each has done, is a matter of record. Influence on a pope, by advisers, donors, governments or orders, is a separate claim and has to be shown case by case with documents. Later parts of this volume do that for money, for the Orders and for Israel.

chapters.label: Part Seven
chapters.title: The Black Nobility and the Orsini
chapters.intro: Part Seven turns from the offices of the Holy See to the families most often said to stand behind them. It explains what the "black nobility" was: the Roman aristocratic houses that took the pope's side after Rome fell to Italy in 1870, with the court offices they held and the record of five of them, the Colonna, Massimo, Torlonia, Pacelli and Orsini. It then sets the documented history of the Orsini against the claims made about them: how many popes the family produced, what its cardinals did, what titles it still holds, and whether it controls the papacy, shares a bloodline with the Rothschilds or supplies a hidden "Grey Pope". It ends with the one modern office that tied the family to the pope, Prince Assistant to the Papal Throne, the removal of Prince Filippo Orsini by Pius XII in January 1958 and the end of hereditary court office under Paul VI in 1968, and asks what, if anything, these families hold today.
chapters.outro: The black nobility was real, and it was a court nobility, not a government. Its families held ceremonial and hereditary offices at the papal court, and the Lateran Concordat of 1929 confirmed their papal titles in Italian law rather than abolishing them. [cite:vt7_wiki_blacknob] [cite:vt7_va_lateran] The Orsini gave the Church three popes, the last of whom died in 1730, not five; their cardinals led opposing blocs in the conclave of 1305; their dukedom of Bracciano was sold before 1698; and no genealogy joins them to the Rothschilds, whose name comes from a house in Frankfurt's Jewish street. [cite:vt7_ce_orsini] [cite:vt7_wiki_conclave1305] [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] [cite:vt7_ra_name] The family's last formal office, Prince Assistant to the Papal Throne, was taken from Filippo Orsini by Pius XII in January 1958, and Paul VI's Pontificalis Domus of 28 March 1968 declared that no office in the Papal Household is hereditary; the last holder of the title died in 2017. [cite:vt7_laj_pa] [cite:vt7_pd_latin] [cite:vt7_br_torlonia] The claims that the Orsini control the papacy, are one bloodline with the Rothschilds, or act as a "Grey Pope" are myths: no document supports them, and the record of 1305, 1958 and 1968 runs against them. Part Eight turns to the bodies that do hold documented institutional weight around the pope: the Society of Jesus, Opus Dei and the Sovereign Order of Malta. [scene:vt8_jesuits|Part Eight: the Jesuits]

sections.h: The Black Nobility: Who They Were
sections.html:
"Black nobility" (nobiltà nera) is the name given to the Roman aristocratic families who sided with the pope after the Italian army entered Rome on 20 September 1870. While Pius IX and his successors called themselves prisoners in the Vatican, these families kept the doors of their Roman palaces closed in mourning, and the term came to cover them and also the people whom the popes ennobled between 1870 and the settlement of 1929. [cite:vt7_wiki_blacknob] The label is modern; the group is old. It grew out of the baronial families of medieval Rome and the families who had served the Papal States and the papal court for centuries. [cite:vt7_wiki_blacknob] How Rome was lost and why the popes refused to accept it is told in [scene:vt2_roman_question|Part Two: the Roman Question].

The first thing to fix about the black nobility is what kind of thing it was. It was a social allegiance, not an organization. It had no charter, no officers, no budget, no membership roll and no seat of its own. A family belonged by choosing the pope's side in a political quarrel with the Kingdom of Italy, and by holding offices and honours at the papal court. The standard list of families still in existence names the Colonna, Massimo, Orsini, Ruspoli, Pallavicini, Theodoli, Sacchetti, Borghese, Odescalchi and Boncompagni-Ludovisi; the Savelli, Caetani, Aldobrandini and Conti are counted among the lines now extinct; members of the Pacelli family, including Eugenio Pacelli, the future Pius XII, are named among its people. [cite:vt7_wiki_blacknob] Anything this volume says about "the black nobility" is therefore a statement about named families and named individuals, each with its own record.

What these families did for the papacy

Their documented role was service at court, not government. Several court offices passed by inheritance in particular families: before the reform of 1968, the office of Marshal of the Holy Roman Church and of the conclave belonged to the Chigi, the Grand Master of the Sacred Apostolic Hospice was a Ruspoli, and the hereditary Quartermaster General of the Apostolic Palace was a Sacchetti. [cite:vt7_wiki_hered] The highest lay honour was the office of Prince Assistant to the Papal Throne, held by the heads of the Orsini and Colonna; it has its own section below ([scene:vt7_prince_assistant_1958|the Prince Assistant and 1958]). Younger sons served in the Noble Guard, founded by Pius VII on 11 May 1801 and recruited from noble families, which stood beside the pope at ceremonies. [cite:vt7_wiki_nobleguard] These were posts of precedence and display. None of them carried authority over the Secretariat of State, over appointments of bishops or over papal finance.

Five families, five records

Colonna. The Colonna gave one pope, Martin V, elected on 11 November 1417, who reigned until his death on 20 February 1431. Sciarra Colonna took part in the assault on Boniface VIII at Anagni in 1303, and Marcantonio II Colonna commanded the papal fleet at Lepanto on 7 October 1571. Julius II's bull Pax Romana of 1511 ended the long feud between the Colonna and the Orsini. [cite:vt7_wiki_colonna] [cite:vt7_audit_brit_martin5] The record shows a family that fought popes as well as served them.

Massimo. The Massimo held the office of the papal posts: Camillo Francesco Massimo (1730–1801) was a papal postmaster, and Francesco Camillo Massimo (1865–1943) was Superintendent General of the Papal Posts. [cite:vt7_wiki_massimo] The family's claim to descend from the Roman general Fabius Maximus goes back to a book of 1556 and is "generally regarded as legendary"; asked by Napoleon whether it was true, a Prince Massimo is reported to have replied that he could not prove it. [cite:vt7_wiki_massimo]

Torlonia. The Torlonia were the newest family on the list and the one most tied to money. Giovanni Torlonia administered Vatican finances and was rewarded with titles: the family's Wikipedia article says Pius VI made him duke of Bracciano in 1794 and Pius VII made him prince of Civitella Cesi in 1803, while the article on the duchy dates the Torlonia purchase of the ducal title and the castle of Bracciano to 1803. [cite:vt7_wiki_torlonia] [cite:vt7_audit_wiki_duchy] The Torlonia bank was the Roman partner in the first Rothschild loan to the Papal States in the early 1830s, which the historian Daniela Felisini describes as made "in partnership with James de Rothschild". [cite:wa_felisini] What the loan documents show and do not show is the subject of [scene:vt11_papal_loans|Part Eleven]. Villa Torlonia, bought by Giovanni Torlonia in 1797, was Mussolini's residence from 1925 to 1943; the city of Rome bought it in 1977. [cite:vt7_mvt_villa] The often-repeated story of a one-lira rent is not stated by the museum and is not confirmed here.

Pacelli. The Pacelli were lawyers, not barons. Marcantonio Pacelli served the papal government, in finance under Gregory XVI and in the interior ministry under Pius IX from 1851 to 1870; his son Filippo was a lawyer of the Rota. [cite:vt7_wiki_pius12early] Filippo's son Francesco Pacelli (1872–1935), dean of the Rota's lawyers, conducted the day-to-day negotiation of the Lateran Pacts with Mussolini's government for Pius XI, alongside Cardinal Gasparri, and was made a marquess by papal brief on 9 June 1929. His three sons were made princes by royal decree in 1941 and 1942, and one of them, Marcantonio, became a brigadier general of the Noble Guard. [cite:vt7_wiki_fpacelli] That Pius XII's brother negotiated the 1929 settlement is documented and worth stating; it does not by itself show any motive for Pius XII's wartime choices, which are examined on their own record in [scene:vt16_war_and_pius_xii|Part Sixteen].

Orsini. The oldest of the families in papal history, and the one around which most of the claims of hidden control gather, has its own section: [scene:vt7_orsini_record|the Orsini record].

1929: what the treaty said about nobles

The Lateran settlement of 11 February 1929 touched the nobility in two places, and neither matches what popular accounts say. Article 42 of the Concordat committed Italy to recognize, by royal decree, noble titles "conferred by the Supreme Pontiffs even after 1870" and those conferred in future. [cite:vt7_va_lateran] Italy then regulated the use of papal titles and decorations by Royal Decree no. 974 of 10 July 1930, limiting applications to Italian and Vatican citizens. [cite:vt7_rd974_1930] Article 10 of the Treaty exempted persons on an agreed list of the Papal Court from Italian military and jury service. [cite:vt7_va_lateran] Vatican citizenship, by contrast, followed residence and office: Article 9 subjects to the Holy See's sovereignty "all persons having stable residence" in Vatican City, and no article names the Roman nobility. [cite:vt7_va_lateran] The treaty did not abolish the noble court positions: it confirmed the papal nobility's titles in Italian law and left the court intact. The statement on Wikipedia that the black nobility received dual citizenship in 1929 is not supported by the treaty text read here. [cite:vt7_wiki_blacknob]

1948 to 1970: how the formal standing ended

The end came from two directions. The Italian Republic's Constitution of 1948 provides in its fourteenth transitional provision that the Republic does not recognize titles of nobility; predicates of titles that existed before 28 October 1922 survive only as part of a surname, and the Constitutional Court confirmed that narrow reading on 26 June 1967. [cite:vt7_cc_101_1967] Inside the Vatican, Paul VI's motu proprio Pontificalis Domus of 28 March 1968 turned the Papal Court into the Papal Household, declared that no office in it was to be regarded as hereditary and reduced the Noble Guard to an honorary cohort. [cite:vt7_pd_latin] Perks such as Vatican number plates were withdrawn. [cite:vt7_wiki_blacknob] In 1970 Paul VI abolished the Noble Guard altogether. [cite:vt7_wiki_nobleguard] Some nobles resented the change, and in 1977 a group led by Princess Elvina Pallavicini began to court the traditionalist Archbishop Marcel Lefebvre, which is to say that part of the old court nobility ended up in open opposition to the reigning pope's line. [cite:vt7_wiki_blacknob]

The description of these families as "the families that owned the papacy" fails on this record. The documented offices were ceremonial; a pope created them, a pope could remove a holder (as Pius XII did in 1958), and a pope abolished their hereditary basis by a single motu proprio in 1968. The families' real influence was the ordinary influence of old Roman wealth: property, marriages, bank boards and access. That is a finding about a social elite. It is not evidence of control.

sections.h: The Orsini: What the Record Shows
sections.html:
The Orsini are one of the oldest families of Rome, and the documented part of their story is remarkable enough without additions. Standard genealogies trace them to an Ursus, count of Tivoli, probably in the ninth century; the family's own tradition of descent from the Julio-Claudian emperors is a legend with no documentary support. [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] They held lands across Lazio and the Kingdom of Naples, fought a feud with the Colonna that Julius II settled by his bull of 1511, and gave the Church popes, cardinals and soldiers. [cite:vt7_wiki_colonna] [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] Popular accounts build a larger structure on this base: five Orsini popes, a hereditary office held for "457 consecutive years", a modern "22nd Duke of Bracciano" in his castle, and a family that "owned the papacy" or stood behind it as a "Grey Pope". This section sets each of those claims against the record. Where a claim fails, it says so and why.

The popes: three, not five

The Catholic Encyclopedia states plainly that "the Orsini gave three popes to the Church": Celestine III (1191–1198), Nicholas III (1277–1280) and Benedict XIII (1724–1730). [cite:vt7_ce_orsini] Wikipedia's article on the family gives the same three and adds, by family tradition, the eighth-century Stephen II and Paul I; those two attributions rest on later genealogical claims about a period before the family appears in documents, and the Catholic Encyclopedia does not count them. [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] The volume therefore uses three.

The popular "five" is not even a fixed five. Versions of it add Nicholas IV "through partial Orsini lineage", Leo XIII, Boniface VIII "through the Caetani", Honorius III or Clement XIII. Each fails on the pope's own birth record. Nicholas IV was Girolamo Masci, born in 1227 at Lisciano near Ascoli; his tie to the Orsini is that Nicholas III had made him a cardinal and that he in turn made Napoleone Orsini a cardinal in 1288, which are appointments, not descent. [cite:vt7_wiki_nicholas4] Leo XIII was Vincenzo Gioacchino Pecci, born at Carpineto Romano in 1810. [cite:vt7_brit_leo13] Clement XIII was Carlo della Torre Rezzonico, of a family that came from Como by way of Genoa to Venice. [cite:vt7_enc_clement13] Honorius III was Cencio, traditionally counted a Savelli, though recent scholarship doubts even that. [cite:vt7_wiki_honorius3] Boniface VIII was Benedetto Caetani of Anagni, and the Caetani are a separate baronial family, not an Orsini branch. [cite:vt7_wiki_boniface8] The confusion may come from Nicholas III's own name: he was Giovanni Gaetani Orsini, son of Matteo Rosso Orsini and of Perna, of the Gaetani family. [cite:vt7_na_nicholas3] That ties the Gaetani to an Orsini pope through his mother; it does not make Boniface VIII an Orsini.

The last Orsini pope, Benedict XIII, died in 1730. [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] In the 296 years since, no member of the family has been elected. A claim that the Orsini "control the papacy" has to account for that gap.

Cardinals and conclaves

Wikipedia counts 34 Orsini cardinals; the figure is given here as reported. [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] The best-documented Orsini intervention in a papal election is the conclave of 1304–1305 at Perugia, which lasted about eleven months and ended on 5 June 1305 with the election of Bertrand de Got as Clement V, the pope who settled in Avignon. Cardinal Napoleone Orsini led the pro-French bloc and his backing was decisive; the opposing bloc was led by another Orsini, Cardinal Matteo Orsini Rosso, together with Boniface VIII's nephew Francesco Caetani. [cite:vt7_wiki_conclave1305] The episode that is offered as proof of Orsini control shows the reverse of a family plan: two Orsini cardinals led the opposing camps.

Nor was Napoleone Orsini a witness at the secret inquiry into the Templar leaders at Chinon in August 1308. The Chinon parchment, found by Barbara Frale in the Vatican archives in September 2001, records an inquiry held from 17 to 20 August 1308 by three cardinals: Bérenger Frédol, Étienne de Suisy and Landolfo Brancacci. [cite:vt7_wiki_chinon] Napoleone Orsini is not among them. The archive and the parchment are discussed in [scene:vt14_apostolic_archive|Part Fourteen].

Titles, castles and the living family

The present head of the family is sometimes styled Duke of Bracciano, and the castle there described as the family's seat. The duchy left the Orsini more than three centuries ago: Flavio Orsini, the last Orsini duke of Bracciano, was forced by debt to sell it to the Odescalchi in 1696 and died on 5 April 1698. [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] [cite:vt7_audit_wiki_duchy] The Torlonia bought the ducal title and the castle in 1803, and the Odescalchi later bought them back; the castle is Odescalchi property. [cite:vt7_audit_wiki_duchy] [cite:vt7_wiki_torlonia] The surviving Orsini line is that of Gravina, whose dukedom dates from 1463 and which became princes of the Empire and Roman princes in 1724. [cite:vt7_ce_orsini] The same sources date the marriage that joined the Orsini to Torlonia money to 1823: the bridegroom was Domenico Orsini (1790–1874), who married Maria Luisa Torlonia. [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] The marriage is real; it joined two Roman families, as such marriages did, and no document links it to the Rothschild loans that followed.

The present head of the family, according to published genealogy, is Domenico Napoleone Orsini, born in 1948, Duke of Gravina; the same source records his brother as heir. [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] He is a private individual. This volume found no document showing him or any living Orsini holding an office at the Holy See, in the Vatican City administration, at the IOR or in the Curia. The last formal office, that of Prince Assistant, was taken from the family in 1958, as the next section shows. [cite:vt7_laj_pa]

Three claims graded

"The Orsini control the papacy." Graded: myth. The claim rests on the family's medieval prominence, a miscount of popes and an office that was ceremonial. It is contradicted by the absence of any Orsini pope since 1730, by the 1305 conclave in which Orsini cardinals led rival blocs, by a pope's removal of the family's head from his court office in 1958 and by a pope's abolition of hereditary court office in 1968. [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] [cite:vt7_wiki_conclave1305] [cite:vt7_pd_latin] No source that makes the claim cites a document showing any Orsini directing a papal decision after 1730.

"Orsini and Rothschild are one bloodline." Graded: myth. The Rothschild name comes from the "House at the Red Shield" in the Jewish street of Frankfurt, where Isaak Elchanan took it in the sixteenth century; Mayer Amschel Rothschild was born there in 1744, and his five sons were ennobled by the Austrian emperor in 1817 and made barons in 1822. [cite:vt7_ra_name] There is no genealogical record joining the Frankfurt family to the Roman one. The claim belongs to a family of stories that presents Rothschild money as the hidden hand behind thrones and popes. Those stories began with eighteenth- and nineteenth-century pamphleteers and were driven by hostility to a Jewish banking family; the historian Mike Rothschild traces how they became a fixture of antisemitic conspiracy theory. [cite:vt7_pw_lasers] The documented contact between the Rothschild houses and Rome is a set of loans to the Papal States from the 1830s, in which the money ran from the bankers to the pope. [cite:wa_ra_naples] [cite:wa_felisini] Those loans are examined in [scene:vt11_papal_loans|Part Eleven] and the alleged "unbroken chain" to 2026 in [scene:vt11_chain_tested|the chain tested].

"The Orsini are the Grey Pope." Graded: myth. The phrase "Grey Pope", sometimes attached to a "Pepe Orsini", has no office, no document and no identifiable holder behind it; even an anonymous web page that spreads it concedes that no verifiable person of that name holds any official role. [cite:vt7_slb_greypope] The wider idea of a hereditary "black nobility" ruling the world through secret committees comes from conspiracy books such as John Coleman's Conspirators' Hierarchy: The Story of the Committee of 300 (1992), whose "aristocratic conspirators" fact-checkers find no credible evidence for. [cite:vt7_md_c300] The "Grey Pope" is examined in full in [scene:vt6_grey_pope_myth|Part Six].

sections.h: The Prince Assistant and the Fall of 1958
sections.html:
The one formal office that tied the Orsini to the person of the pope in modern times was that of Prince Assistant to the Papal Throne (Principe Assistente al Soglio Pontificio). Its history is the clearest test of how much power the old Roman families held, because it has a beginning, a documented holder, a documented removal and a documented end. Popular accounts of it give incompatible dates and lengths of tenure. This section rebuilds the timeline from the sources.

What the office was

The office is believed to have been instituted by Julius II in 1511, the year of his bull ending the Orsini–Colonna feud, and it was the highest honour a layman could hold at the papal court. [cite:vt7_laj_pa] [cite:vt7_wiki_colonna] It could be granted to an individual, but it belonged by hereditary right to the heads of the Colonna and the Orsini. The rule that the two families would share it in alternation was set by Benedict XIII, himself an Orsini pope (1724–1730); the sources give the Orsini tenure as running "from 1735 until 1958". [cite:vt7_laj_pa] [cite:vt7_wiki_pa] The Catholic Encyclopedia, written in the early twentieth century, says simply that the head of the Orsini "always enjoys the dignity of assistant at the papal throne". [cite:vt7_ce_orsini]

The duties were ceremonial. A Prince Assistant served under the Prefect of the Apostolic Palace, did the honours of the house at solemn civil ceremonies such as the reception of sovereigns, heads of state and ambassadors presenting their credentials, stood beside the papal throne at great liturgies, and took precedence immediately after the College of Cardinals. [cite:vt7_laj_pa] [cite:vt7_wiki_pa] Nothing in the description of the office gave its holder a vote, a signature or a budget. Its value was proximity and rank. The office dates from 1511, and the Orsini shared it with the Colonna rather than holding it alone.

January 1958: a pope removes a prince

Filippo Orsini (1920–1984), head of the Gravina line, held the title from 1950. [cite:vt7_wiki_orsini] In 1957, while the British actress Belinda Lee was filming in Italy, the two began a much-reported affair; both were married to other people, and Lee left her husband in September 1957. [cite:vt7_wiki_blee] In late January 1958 Italian newspapers reported that Lee had taken an overdose of sleeping pills; three days later Orsini was reported in hospital with cuts to his wrists. Lee said the overdose was an accident, and Orsini would not tell the police why he had hurt himself. [cite:vt7_wiki_blee] The Vatican let it be known that he would lose his title if it were proven that he had attempted suicide. [cite:vt7_wiki_blee]

In January 1958 Pius XII removed Filippo Orsini from the office of Prince Assistant; TIME reported the case under the headline "The Papal Prince" on 10 February 1958. [cite:vt7_laj_pa] On 19 February 1958 the London Daily Mail reported that the pope had condemned suicide in a speech that was widely read as a reference to the scandal, although neither Orsini nor Lee was named. [cite:vt7_wiki_blee] Lee left Rome in February 1958; by December the couple were reported to be living together in Paris; she announced the end of the relationship in December 1959, and she died in a car crash in California on 12 March 1961. [cite:vt7_wiki_blee]

The episode matters for this volume for one reason: it shows the direction of power. A pope removed the head of the oldest family of the black nobility from its last court office because of his private conduct, and the family had no recourse. The removal was a disciplinary act within a court the pope controlled. It is the opposite of what the "Orsini control the papacy" claim predicts.

After 1958: Torlonia, then the end of inheritance

The office did not pass to another Orsini. The sources disagree on when the second chair was filled: the Liturgical Arts Journal says John XXIII appointed Prince Alessandro Torlonia in 1962, to restore the complement of two for the Second Vatican Council, while Wikipedia's article on the Torlonia gives 1958. [cite:vt7_laj_pa] [cite:vt7_wiki_torlonia] This volume leaves the date open. Either way, the new holder came from the banking family that the papacy had ennobled at the turn of the nineteenth century, not from the old baronial line. [cite:vt7_wiki_torlonia]

Ten years later Paul VI ended the hereditary basis of every court office. His motu proprio Pontificalis Domus, dated 28 March 1968, reorganized the Papal Court as the Papal Household, divided into a Papal Chapel and a Papal Family, and declared that in the Papal Household "no office whatever is to be regarded as hereditary" (nullum prorsus munus est veluti hereditarium existimandum). [cite:vt7_pd_latin] The same document suppressed a long list of court posts, among them the Palatine Cardinals, the Master of the Horse, the General Superintendent of the Posts and the hereditary Quartermaster General, and kept the Prince Assistants in the Papal Family. [cite:vt7_wiki_pd] The two living holders, Aspreno Colonna and Alessandro Torlonia, were allowed to keep the title for life; Colonna died in 1987, and Torlonia, president of the family's Banca del Fucino, died at the end of December 2017. [cite:vt7_laj_pa] [cite:vt7_br_torlonia] The title has not been conferred since and has not been formally suppressed. [cite:vt7_wiki_pa]

The office was not abolished by the Lateran Treaty of 1929: it was held and filled after 1929, its Orsini holder was removed in 1958, and its hereditary basis was ended in 1968. Nor does any document found make the 1958 scandal the catalyst for the reform of 1968: Pontificalis Domus reformed the whole court in the period after the Second Vatican Council, presents itself as a reorganization to stress the pope's "essentially spiritual" mission alongside his civic and international role, and does not refer to the Orsini case. [cite:vt7_wiki_pd] The two events are ten years apart and the second applies to every court family, not to one.

What the families hold now

As of October 2026, the record shows no member of the Orsini, Colonna, Torlonia, Massimo or any other black-nobility family holding a hereditary or ex officio post at the Holy See. [cite:vt7_wiki_pa] [cite:vt7_pd_latin] What these families keep is what old Roman wealth keeps anywhere: names, palaces, art collections, marriages and in some cases banks, which are private property and private influence, not offices of the Holy See. How the Holy See is in fact governed, by the pope and the Curia under the 2022 constitution, is the subject of [scene:vt6_curia_2022|Part Six]; how its money is run is the subject of [scene:vt9_ior|Part Nine].

chapters.label: Part Eight
chapters.title: Orders and a Second Sovereign: Jesuits, Opus Dei, Malta
chapters.intro: Part Eight examines the three Catholic bodies most often named as powers behind the pope: the Society of Jesus, Opus Dei and the Sovereign Order of Malta. Each is a real institution with a documented history, a known size and a legal relationship to the Holy See that can be read in papal bulls, decrees and treaties. The part sets out how the Jesuits were founded, abolished by one pope and restored by another, and what they run today; how Opus Dei rose to a unique status in Church law under John Paul II and was reduced under Francis, and what its critics and the organisation itself say about its treatment of members; and how a pilgrims' hospital in Jerusalem became a sovereign body without territory that exchanges ambassadors with more than a hundred states and still answers to the pope as a religious order. For each, the claims that circulate about hidden control are graded against those documents.
chapters.outro: The three bodies are each tied to the pope, and each tie runs from the pope downward. The Jesuits vow obedience to the pope "with regard to missions"; a pope abolished the order in 1773, another restored it in 1814, and John Paul II overrode its leadership in 1981; it has shrunk from 36,038 members in 1965 to 13,768 in 2025, and its first pope, Francis, was succeeded by an Augustinian. [cite:vt6_gc35_d4] [cite:vt8_wiki_suppr] [cite:vt8_wiki_sollicitudo] [cite:vt8_am_kolvenbach] [cite:vt8_ch_sj] Opus Dei, about 93,000 members by its own count, was moved to the Dicastery for the Clergy and its prelate barred from episcopal rank by Francis in 2022; its revised statutes still awaited papal approval as of October 2026, and a criminal investigation in Argentina that it denies had produced no charges by September 2026. [cite:vt8_od_members] [cite:vt8_va_charisma] [cite:vt8_ncr_leo_statutes] [cite:vt8_lcmdp_2026] The Order of Malta is a sovereign without territory, recognised by 118 countries by its own count and a UN General Assembly observer since 1994, yet as a religious order it "depends … on the Holy See", as Francis's removal of its Grand Master in 2017 and his imposed constitution of 2022 showed. [cite:vt8_om_diplomacy] [cite:vt8_un_48_265] [cite:vt8_cna_festing] [cite:vt8_va_smom2022] None of the three controls the Holy See. Part Nine turns from the orders to the money: the IOR, APSA, the Governorate and Peter's Pence. [scene:vt9_ior|Part Nine: the IOR]

sections.h: The Society of Jesus: an Order Under the Pope
sections.html:
The Society of Jesus is the body most often cast as the hidden hand behind the papacy. Part Six tested the "Black Pope" nickname and the office of the Jesuit Superior General against the record. [scene:vt6_black_pope|Part Six: the "Black Pope"] This section sets out the order itself: how it was founded, what its members promise and to whom, how a pope abolished it and another restored it, how large it is now, what it runs and what it does not, and what changed and did not change when one of its members became pope in 2013.

Founding: from a vow in Paris to a papal bull

The order began as a group of students. On 15 August 1534 Ignatius of Loyola, a Basque former soldier, and six companions, among them Francis Xavier, Diego Laínez and Peter Faber, took vows of poverty and chastity in a chapel at Montmartre, outside Paris. They called themselves the Compañía de Jesús. The date often given as the order's foundation is therefore the date of a private vow; the order existed in Church law only from 27 September 1540, when Pope Paul III approved it, and Ignatius was chosen as its first Superior General. [cite:vt8_wiki_sj]

The approving bull, Regimini militantis Ecclesiae, carried the group's own charter, the Formula of the Institute. It limited the Society to sixty members and bound Jesuits to accept any mission the pope gave them through their superior, rather than arranging missions with the pope directly. The limit on numbers was lifted by Julius III's bull Exposcit debitum of 21 July 1550, which gave the order its final approval. [cite:vt8_wiki_regimini] The military language of the charter, which speaks of serving as "a soldier of God beneath the banner of the Cross", has often been read as describing an army. It describes a religious order whose members take vows and are sent where their superiors decide. [cite:vt8_wiki_sj]

The fourth vow, and the vows against ambition

Members of most Catholic religious orders take three vows: poverty, chastity and obedience. Jesuits who reach full incorporation, the "professed", take a fourth, of special obedience to the pope concerning missions. James Martin, a Jesuit writer, explains it as a commitment to go wherever the pope sends them, because Ignatius believed the pope had the widest view of where the Church needed workers; the historian John O'Malley describes it as a vow about worldwide mobility. [cite:vt8_am_vows] The Society's 35th General Congregation restated in 2008 that the vow's whole purpose "was and is with regard to missions". [cite:vt6_gc35_d4]

The professed then take five further private vows. Three of them concern ambition: not to seek Church dignities such as a bishopric, not to seek high office in the Society, and to report any Jesuit who does. [cite:vt8_am_vows] These are the founding documents that conspiracy writing about the order most often leaves out. Read as written, they bind Jesuits to the pope's direction and bar them from campaigning for the offices through which the Church is governed.

Expelled by kings, abolished by a pope, restored by a pope

The order's greatest crisis came from Catholic monarchies, not Protestant ones. Portugal expelled the Jesuits in 1759 and deported about a thousand to the Papal States; France dissolved the Society in 1764; Spain and Naples expelled it in 1767, and Parma in 1768. Under pressure from those courts, Pope Clement XIV issued the brief Dominus ac Redemptor on 21 July 1773, which declared: "we abolish and suppress the oft-mentioned Society". [cite:vt8_wiki_suppr] The Superior General of the day, Lorenzo Ricci, died a prisoner in the papal fortress of Castel Sant'Angelo in 1775. [cite:vt6_wiki_ricci]

The order survived because two non-Catholic rulers refused to publish the papal brief. Catherine II of Russia kept the Jesuits in her newly annexed Belarusian lands and allowed them a novitiate, and Frederick II of Prussia barred the brief's distribution for some years. [cite:vt8_wiki_suppr] Pope Pius VII restored the Society throughout the Church by the bull Sollicitudo omnium ecclesiarum of 7 August 1814. [cite:vt8_wiki_sollicitudo] The order's legal existence was ended by one papal act and restored by another, forty-one years apart.

How large it is now

The Society is the largest male religious order in the Catholic Church, but it is about a third of the size it was sixty years ago. Figures drawn from the Holy See's yearbook, the Annuario Pontificio, give a peak of 36,038 members in 1965 and 1966, then a steady fall: 14,839 in 2021, 14,195 in 2023 and 13,768 in 2025, of whom 9,987 were priests. [cite:vt8_ch_sj] The Society's own count for 1 January 2022 was 14,439 Jesuits: 10,432 priests, 2,587 scholastics in training, 837 brothers and 583 novices. [cite:vt8_sj_numbers2022] The figure of 17,000 members still found in some accounts is out of date by more than a decade.

The order is governed from its General Curia in Rome by a Superior General elected for life by a General Congregation of delegates, through provincial superiors he appoints. [cite:vt8_wiki_sj] [cite:vt6_wiki_supgen] As of October 2026 the Superior General was Arturo Sosa Abascal, a Venezuelan elected on 14 October 2016; on 16 October 2026 the Ghana News Agency reported his visit to Accra, and no convocation of a 37th General Congregation, which would be needed to elect a successor, was found. [cite:vt8_gna_sosa2026] [cite:vt6_wiki_gc]

What it runs, and what it does not

The Society's weight lies in education. The Jesuit education networks' own 2024 count lists 177 universities in the International Association of Jesuit Universities, 937 schools in the Jesuit Global Network of Schools, 388 schools of the Jesuit Refugee Service and 2,127 schools of Fe y Alegría, a popular-education movement founded by a Jesuit: 3,629 institutions in all. [cite:vt8_em_map2024] Other figures in circulation (190, "200+", 228, "250+" universities) count by different definitions or have no source; Part Thirteen examines the universities in detail. [scene:vt13_jesuit_universities|Part Thirteen: the Jesuit universities]

A Jesuit school is not necessarily a school the order owns or controls. In the United States, control of several leading Catholic universities passed in the late 1960s from the religious orders that founded them to independent boards of trustees made up mostly of lay men and women, and that became the norm across Catholic higher education in the 1970s. Joseph O'Hare, a Jesuit and former president of Fordham, described the change as a response to institutional complexity and to fewer, older religious. [cite:vt8_am_ohare2007] The order's influence in such institutions runs through sponsorship, mission and the Jesuits who work there, not through ownership.

The Society holds no office in the government of the Holy See. Individual Jesuits have served in the Curia, as cardinals and as editors of papal publications, but they do so as appointees of the pope, removable by him, and the order as such has no seat in the Secretariat of State or any dicastery. [cite:vt6_gc_curia] When the pope and the order have disagreed, the record shows the pope prevailing: after Superior General Pedro Arrupe suffered a stroke on 7 August 1981, John Paul II set aside the vicar general Arrupe had chosen, Vincent O'Keefe, and installed two Jesuits of his own choosing, Paolo Dezza and Giuseppe Pittau; the order was allowed to elect a successor only two years later. [cite:vt8_am_kolvenbach]

The first Jesuit pope

Jorge Mario Bergoglio entered the Jesuit novitiate in Buenos Aires on 11 March 1958, was ordained on 13 December 1969 and led the Argentine province from 1973. He became a bishop in 1992 and a cardinal on 21 February 2001, and was elected pope on 13 March 2013, taking the name Francis. [cite:vt8_va_francis_bio] He was the first Jesuit to become pope, 473 years after the order's approval. [cite:vt8_usccb_francis] His election shows a Jesuit reaching the papacy once; it does not show the order steering the conclave, and a Jesuit pope had taken the vow not to seek such office. Francis died on 21 April 2025, and the conclave of May 2025 elected Robert Prevost, an Augustinian, as Leo XIV. [cite:vt6_wiki_conclave2025] [cite:vt6_vn_leobio]

The myths, graded

The idea of a secret Jesuit plan is older than most of the order's schools. Its first famous text, the Monita Secreta ("secret instructions"), appeared in Kraków in 1614 or 1615, presented as the order's hidden rules for winning wealth and influence. Its likely author was Jerome Zahorowski, a Polish Jesuit expelled from the Society in 1613, and many scholars, as well as the British Museum's cataloguers, have treated it as a forgery. [cite:vt8_wiki_monita] Modern versions add that the order rules the world "through their Jewish and Masonic proxies", which joins an anti-Catholic theory to an antisemitic one. [cite:vt6_splc_phelps] The table grades the main claims against the documents.

The Society's own position, stated by its General Congregation, is that its distinctive bond is availability to the pope for mission. [cite:vt6_gc35_d4] The documented record is consistent with that statement: an order large in schools and universities, shrinking in members, and subject to papal decisions it did not choose.

sections.h: Opus Dei: a Prelature, Its Critics and a Pope's Reform
sections.html:
Opus Dei is younger than the Jesuits by almost four centuries and much smaller in priests, but it carries a reputation for quiet influence that rivals theirs. Its reputation comes from three sources: its unusual legal form inside the Church, the public careers of some of its members, and the testimony of former members. This section takes each in turn, sets out how Pope Francis reduced its standing in Church law in 2022 and 2023, and places the criticism beside the organisation's own stated position.

From a Madrid foundation to a personal prelature

Josemaría Escrivá, a Spanish priest, founded Opus Dei ("the Work of God") in Madrid on 2 October 1928. Its message was that ordinary lay people could seek holiness through their daily work, without becoming monks, nuns or priests. The Holy See approved it as a secular institute, provisionally in 1947 and definitively in 1950 under Pius XII. [cite:vt8_wiki_opus]
